arguments.name: name
arguments.description: Name of the DHCP client. If not set, RouterOS generates a name, for example `client1`.

arguments.name: interface
arguments.description: Interface the DHCP client runs on. The received IP address is added to this interface as a dynamic address.

arguments.name: add-default-route
arguments.description:
Which routes received from the DHCP server to add to the routing table.
- `yes` (default) - Add the classless static routes (option 121) when the server sends them, otherwise a default route through the received gateway (option 3). When option 121 is present, the gateway from option 3 is ignored.
- `special-classless` - Add both the classless static routes and a default route through the received gateway.
- `no` - Do not add routes.

arguments.name: default-route-distance
arguments.description: Distance of the routes the client adds. Default: 1.

arguments.name: default-route-tables
arguments.description: Routing tables to add the routes to, as `table` or `table:distance` entries. A distance given here overrides `default-route-distance` for that table. `default` is the main routing table, or the VRF routing table when the client interface belongs to a VRF. Default: default.

arguments.name: check-gateway
arguments.description: Gateway check set on the routes the client adds (`none`, `arp`, `ping` or `bfd`), so a route is only used while its gateway responds. See [gateway reachability](/docs/7.25/user-guides/routing-and-networking-protocols/routing-decision). Default: none.

arguments.name: use-peer-dns
arguments.description: Whether to use the DNS servers received from the DHCP server. They are added to the dynamic servers of the DNS resolver (`/ip/dns`). Default: yes.

arguments.name: use-peer-ntp
arguments.description: Whether to use the NTP servers received from the DHCP server. They are added as dynamic entries to the NTP client servers (`/system/ntp/client/servers`). Default: yes.

arguments.name: allow-reconfigure
arguments.description: Whether to accept Reconfigure (FORCERENEW) messages from the DHCP server. When enabled, the client asks for a reconfigure key when it binds, and the server sends the key in its reply. The key authenticates the server's Reconfigure messages (RFC 6704, HMAC-MD5). On a Reconfigure message, the client renews its lease immediately. The server can only send Reconfigure messages to clients that bound with this setting enabled. Default: no.

arguments.name: vlan-priority
arguments.description: Priority Code Point (PCP, 0-7) set in the VLAN header of the packets the client sends. Applies only when the client runs on a VLAN interface.

arguments.name: dscp
arguments.description: DSCP value (0-63) set in the IP header of the packets the client sends. When not set, packets are sent with DSCP 0.

arguments.name: use-broadcast
arguments.description:
Whether the client sets the broadcast flag in DHCPDISCOVER and DHCPREQUEST messages, which asks the server to broadcast its replies. Renewal requests are sent as unicast and never set the flag.
- `both` (default) - Set the flag during the first 15 seconds of getting an address, then continue without it.
- `always` - Always set the flag.
- `never` - Never set the flag.

arguments.name: dhcp-options
arguments.description: Options the client sends to the DHCP server, selected by name from `/ip/dhcp-client/option`. The predefined `clientid` and `clientid_duid` options both use code 61: `clientid` identifies the client by the MAC address of its interface, `clientid_duid` by the router's DUID (RFC 4361), the same DUID the DHCPv6 client uses. Default: hostname,clientid.

arguments.name: script
arguments.description:
Script to run when the client gets a lease and when it loses or releases it. The script receives these variables:
- `bound` - `1` when a lease was obtained, `0` when it was lost or released.
- `server-address` - IP address of the DHCP server.
- `lease-address` - IP address from the lease.
- `interface` - Name of the client interface.
- `gateway-address` - Gateway received from the server.
- `vendor-specific` - Value of the vendor-specific information option (option 43) received from the server.
- `lease-options` - Array of the options received from the server, indexed by option code. Values of binary options are hex strings.

flags.name: I
flags.description: The DHCP client configuration is invalid.

flags.name: D
flags.description: The DHCP client was created dynamically.

readOnlyArguments.name: custom-source-mac-address
readOnlyArguments.description: Custom source MAC address used by the DHCP client.

readOnlyArguments.name: custom-hostname-suffix
readOnlyArguments.description: Suffix appended to the hostname sent to the DHCP server.

readOnlyArguments.name: status
readOnlyArguments.type: enum (stopped | searching... | requesting... | bound | renewing... | rebinding... | error) { stopped:0, searching...:1, requesting...:2, bound:3, renewing...:4, rebinding...:5, error:6 }
readOnlyArguments.description:
Current state of the client:
- `searching...` - Sending DHCPDISCOVER messages and waiting for an offer.
- `requesting...` - Requesting an offered address.
- `bound` - The client has a lease.
- `renewing...` - Renewing the lease with the server that issued it, from half of the lease time.
- `rebinding...` - The server did not answer the renewal. Requesting the lease from any server, from 87.5% of the lease time.
- `stopped` - The client is disabled.
- `error` - The client cannot run.

readOnlyArguments.name: address
readOnlyArguments.description: IP address and prefix length received from the DHCP server.

readOnlyArguments.name: netmask
readOnlyArguments.description: Subnet mask received from the DHCP server.

readOnlyArguments.name: gateway
readOnlyArguments.description: Gateway received from the DHCP server (option 3).

readOnlyArguments.name: dhcp-server
readOnlyArguments.description: IP address of the DHCP server that issued the lease.

readOnlyArguments.name: primary-dns
readOnlyArguments.description: First DNS server received from the DHCP server.

readOnlyArguments.name: secondary-dns
readOnlyArguments.description: Second DNS server received from the DHCP server.

readOnlyArguments.name: primary-ntp
readOnlyArguments.description: First NTP server received from the DHCP server.

readOnlyArguments.name: secondary-ntp
readOnlyArguments.description: Second NTP server received from the DHCP server.

readOnlyArguments.name: caps-managers
readOnlyArguments.description: CAPsMAN addresses received from the DHCP server (option 138).

readOnlyArguments.name: reconfigure-key
readOnlyArguments.description: Key received from the DHCP server to authenticate its Reconfigure messages (RFC 6704, HMAC-MD5). Set only when `allow-reconfigure` is enabled.

readOnlyArguments.name: reconfigure-last-counter
readOnlyArguments.description: Replay-detection counter of the last Reconfigure message accepted from the DHCP server. It starts at 0 when the client binds and increases with every Reconfigure message.

readOnlyArguments.name: expires-after
readOnlyArguments.description: Time until the lease expires.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: Name of the option, used in the `dhcp-options` property of the client.

arguments.name: code
arguments.description: DHCP option code (1-254), or one of the names `hostname` (12), `vendor-specific` (43), `vendor-class-id` (60) or `client-id` (61).

arguments.name: value
arguments.description:
Value of the option, in the same syntax as DHCP server option values. The value can contain these variables:
- `$(HOSTNAME)` - The router's identity.
- `$(CLIENT_MAC)` - MAC address of the client interface.
- `$(CLIENT_DUID)` - The router's DUID, the same DUID the DHCPv6 client uses.

readOnlyArguments.name: raw-value
readOnlyArguments.description: The option value as it is sent, in hex.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: Name of the relay.

arguments.name: interface
arguments.description: Interface on which the relay listens for DHCP requests from clients.

arguments.name: dhcp-server-vrf
arguments.description: VRF in which the DHCP servers are reached. When it differs from the VRF of `interface`, the replies of the server, which are sent to `local-address`, must be brought into this VRF, for example with a dst-nat rule. Default: main.

arguments.name: dhcp-server
arguments.description: DHCP servers to forward requests to. The relay forwards every request to all of them.

arguments.name: delay-threshold
arguments.description: Minimum value of the seconds-elapsed field (`secs`) a request must have to be forwarded, so the relay forwards only clients that have been trying for that long. With `none`, all requests are forwarded. Default: none.

arguments.name: local-address
arguments.description: Address the relay writes into the gateway address field (`giaddr`) of forwarded requests. The DHCP server sends its replies to this address and selects the server by its `relay` property. With `0.0.0.0`, an address of `interface` is used. Default: 0.0.0.0.

arguments.name: add-relay-info
arguments.description: Whether to add relay agent information (option 82) to forwarded requests. The circuit ID is the MAC address of `interface`, and the remote ID is the MAC address of the client, or `relay-info-remote-id` when it is set. Default: no.

arguments.name: relay-info-remote-id
arguments.description: Text to send as the remote ID in option 82 instead of the MAC address of the client. Used only with `add-relay-info=yes`.

arguments.name: local-address-as-src-ip
arguments.description: Whether to send forwarded requests from `local-address` instead of from the address of the interface towards the server. Default: no.

flags.name: X
flags.description: The relay is disabled. New relays are created disabled.

readOnlyArguments.name: requests
readOnlyArguments.description: Number of client requests the relay forwarded to the servers.

readOnlyArguments.name: responses
readOnlyArguments.description: Number of server replies the relay delivered to clients.

arguments.name: interface
arguments.description: Interface to watch for DHCP servers.

arguments.name: valid-server
arguments.description: MAC addresses of the DHCP servers that are allowed on the interface. Replies from other servers raise an alert.

arguments.name: on-alert
arguments.description: Script to run when an unknown DHCP server is detected.

arguments.name: alert-timeout
arguments.description: Time after which a detected server is forgotten. If the server is still present afterwards, a new alert is raised. With `none`, detected servers are never forgotten. Default: 1h.

flags.name: X
flags.description: The alert is disabled. New alerts are created disabled.

readOnlyArguments.name: unknown-server
readOnlyArguments.description: MAC addresses of the unknown DHCP servers that were detected.

arguments.name: store-leases-disk
arguments.description: How often leases are saved to disk: a time interval, `immediately`, or `never`. Saving less often reduces writes to the flash storage. Default: 5m.

arguments.name: accounting
arguments.description: Whether to send RADIUS accounting for the leases of servers that use RADIUS (`use-radius`). Default: yes.

arguments.name: interim-update
arguments.description: Interval of RADIUS interim accounting updates. Default: 0s.

arguments.name: radius-password
arguments.description: Password sent in RADIUS Access-Request messages: `empty`, `same-as-user` (the user name, which is the MAC address of the client), or a fixed password. Default: empty.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: Name of the DHCP server.

arguments.name: interface
arguments.description: Interface the DHCP server listens on. The interface must have an IP address, otherwise the server is invalid. Only one server for directly connected clients can run on an interface; more servers on the same interface must each have a different `relay` address.

arguments.name: relay
arguments.description:
Which requests the server answers, by the gateway address (`giaddr`) of the request:
- `0.0.0.0` (default) - Only requests from directly connected clients, no relayed requests.
- `255.255.255.255` - Requests from any DHCP relay, except those answered by another server that has this relay's address set.
- An IP address - Only requests relayed by the DHCP relay with this address, which is the relay's `local-address`.

arguments.name: lease-time
arguments.description: How long a lease lasts. Clients renew the lease after half of this time and start rebinding after 87.5% of it. Static leases without their own `lease-time` also use this value. Default: 30m.

arguments.name: address-pool
arguments.description: IP pool to give out dynamic addresses from. With `static-only`, the server only answers clients that have a static lease. Default: static-only.

arguments.name: dynamic-lease-identifiers
arguments.description: Identifiers the server uses to recognize a client for dynamic leases: `client-mac` (the hardware address), `client-id` (option 61) and `opt-82` (relay agent information). A client that changes a selected identifier gets a new lease. Default: client-mac,client-id.

arguments.name: bootp-support
arguments.description:
How the server answers BOOTP clients:
- `none` - Do not answer BOOTP requests.
- `static` (default) - Offer only static leases to BOOTP clients.
- `dynamic` - Offer static and dynamic leases to BOOTP clients.

arguments.name: bootp-lease-time
arguments.description: Lease time for BOOTP clients: `forever` (default) for leases that never expire, `lease-time` to use the `lease-time` of the server, or a time value.

arguments.name: delay-threshold
arguments.description: Minimum value of the seconds-elapsed field (`secs`) a request must have to be answered. The client sets this field to the time since it started getting or renewing an address, so a threshold makes the server answer only clients that have been trying for that long, for example to let another server answer first. With `none`, all requests are answered. Default: none.

arguments.name: server-address
arguments.description: Address the server uses as its identity: replies are sent from this address and carry it as the server identifier (option 54). When not set, the address of the server interface is used. Set it when the interface has several addresses.

arguments.name: add-arp
arguments.description: Whether to add a permanent ARP entry for the address of each bound lease, shown with the `H` flag in `/ip/arp`. Use it when the interface does not resolve ARP itself, for example with ARP mode `reply-only`. Default: no.

arguments.name: add-dns-entries
arguments.description: Whether to add a dynamic DNS entry (`/ip/dns/static`, type A) for the address of each bound lease. The entry name is the host name the client sends (option 12) followed by `add-dns-entries-suffix`, and its TTL is the lease time. The router's DNS resolver answers these names. Default: no.

arguments.name: add-dns-entries-suffix
arguments.description: Domain appended to the client host name in the DNS entries created by `add-dns-entries`, for example `laptop.lan`. Used only with `add-dns-entries=yes`. When the network has no `domain`, the server also sends this suffix as the domain name (option 15). It cannot be empty. Default: lan.

arguments.name: authoritative
arguments.description:
How the server answers requests for addresses it cannot give, so that such clients start over sooner:
- `yes` (default) - Answer with DHCPNAK.
- `no` - Ignore broadcast requests for such addresses, for example from a rebinding client, so another server can answer them.
- `after-2sec-delay`, `after-10sec-delay` - For broadcast requests, behave as `no` while the `secs` field of the request is below 2 or 10 seconds, and as `yes` after that. To ignore all requests below a threshold, use `delay-threshold`.
Unicast renewal requests are always answered: with DHCPNAK when the requested address cannot be given, or with a new lease when that address is free in the pool.

arguments.name: always-broadcast
arguments.description: Whether to broadcast replies even when the client has not set the broadcast flag. With `no`, replies follow the client's broadcast flag. Default: no.

arguments.name: use-radius
arguments.description:
Whether to use a RADIUS server (a `/radius` entry with `service=dhcp`) for leases:
- `no` (default) - Do not use RADIUS.
- `yes` - Authorize leases and send accounting through RADIUS. While the server waits for the RADIUS reply, the lease has the `authorizing` status and the client gets no address.
- `accounting` - Use RADIUS for accounting only.

arguments.name: client-mac-limit
arguments.description: Maximum number of leases that clients with the same MAC address can get. Default: unlimited.

arguments.name: conflict-detection
arguments.description: Whether to check an address with ARP and ICMP before offering it. When another host answers, the server logs a warning, keeps the address as a lease with the `conflict` status for the lease time, and offers another free address. Addresses of static leases are not checked. Default: yes.

arguments.name: use-framed-as-classless
arguments.description: Whether to send the Framed-Route attributes received from RADIUS to the client as classless static routes (option 121). When both Framed-Route and Classless-Static-Route are received, Classless-Static-Route is used. Default: yes.

arguments.name: use-reconfigure
arguments.description: Whether the server supports Reconfigure (FORCERENEW) messages. When enabled, the server gives a reconfigure key to clients that ask for one, for example a RouterOS DHCP client with `allow-reconfigure=yes`, and the `send-reconfigure` command of the lease makes such a client renew its lease. Reconfigure messages are sent only by that command, not when server or network settings change. Without this setting, clients get no key and `send-reconfigure` is refused. Default: no.

arguments.name: lease-script
arguments.description:
Script to run when a lease is bound, and when it is released or expires. The script receives these variables:
- `leaseBound` - `1` when the lease was bound, `0` when it was released or expired.
- `leaseServerName` - Name of the DHCP server.
- `leaseActMAC` - MAC address of the client.
- `leaseActIP` - IP address of the lease.
- `lease-hostname` - Host name sent by the client.
- `lease-options` - Array of the options sent to the client, indexed by option code.
- `lease-agent-circuit-id`, `lease-agent-remote-id` - Circuit ID and remote ID from the relay agent information option (option 82), when the request came through a relay that adds it.

arguments.name: insert-queue-before
arguments.description: Where to place the dynamic simple queues created for leases with a `rate-limit`: `first` (default) at the top of `/queue/simple`, `bottom` at the end, or before the named queue.

arguments.name: parent-queue
arguments.description: Parent of the dynamic simple queues created for leases with a `rate-limit`. Default: none.

arguments.name: dhcp-option-set
arguments.description: Option set (`/ip/dhcp-server/option/sets`) to send to the clients of this server. Options of a lease take precedence over those of the server, and options of the server over those of the network. Default: none.

arguments.name: address-lists
arguments.description: Firewall address lists to which the address of each bound lease is added as a dynamic entry. The entry is removed when the lease ends.

arguments.name: allow-dual-stack-queue
arguments.description: Whether a lease and a DHCPv6 binding of the same client share one dynamic simple queue, which then contains both the IPv4 and the IPv6 address. The client is recognized by its MAC address and DUID. The DHCPv6 server must have this setting enabled as well. Default: yes.

arguments.name: support-broadband-tr101
arguments.description: Pass additional Option 82 Suboptions to RADIUS server as described in RFC 4679 and The Broadband Forum TR-101

arguments.name: ipv6-only-preferred
arguments.description: Whether to send the IPv6-Only Preferred option (option 108, RFC 8925) to clients that request it. A client that requests the option then gets no IPv4 address: the offer contains the option and no address, so a supporting client uses IPv6 only. The option carries a wait time of 0 seconds, which RFC 8925 clients raise to the minimum of 300 seconds before they try IPv4 again. Default: no.

flags.name: D
flags.description: The DHCP server was created dynamically.

flags.name: I
flags.description: The DHCP server configuration is invalid, for example because its interface has no IP address.

arguments.name: address
arguments.description: IP address of a static lease, or the name of an IP pool to give the client an address from. With `0.0.0.0`, the address pool of the server is used.

arguments.name: mac-address
arguments.description: MAC address of the client the static lease is for.

arguments.name: use-src-mac
arguments.description: Whether to identify the client by the source MAC address of its packets instead of the client hardware address field (`chaddr`) of the DHCP message.

arguments.name: client-id
arguments.description: Client identifier (option 61) of the client the static lease is for, in the format shown in `active-client-id`, for example `1:4e:97:a1:4c:d1:38`.

arguments.name: rate-limit
arguments.description:
Bandwidth limit for the client, as `rx-rate[/tx-rate] [rx-burst-rate[/tx-burst-rate] [rx-burst-threshold[/tx-burst-threshold] [rx-burst-time[/tx-burst-time]]]]`. Rates are in bits per second, with an optional `k` or `M` suffix, and missing tx values are taken from the rx values. Only static leases can have a rate limit.
The server creates a dynamic simple queue named `dhcp-ds` for the address of the lease, with this limit as `limit-at` and `max-limit`.

arguments.name: routes
arguments.description: Routes the server adds while the lease is bound, as `dst-address/mask gateway distance` entries separated by commas, for example `10.77.0.0/24 172.31.255.105 5`.

arguments.name: insert-queue-before
arguments.description: Where to place the dynamic simple queue created for this lease: `first` (default) at the top of `/queue/simple`, `bottom` at the end, or before the named queue.

arguments.name: parent-queue
arguments.description: Parent of the dynamic simple queue created for this lease. Default: none.

arguments.name: queue-type
arguments.description: Queue type of the dynamic simple queue created for this lease.

arguments.name: address-lists
arguments.description: Firewall address lists to which the address of the lease is added while the lease is bound.

arguments.name: server
arguments.description: DHCP server the lease belongs to. With `all`, the static lease is valid on every server.

arguments.name: block-access
arguments.description: Whether to block the client: the server does not answer it, and the lease gets the `B` flag. Default: no.

arguments.name: allow-dual-stack-queue
arguments.description: Whether this lease and a DHCPv6 binding of the same client share one dynamic simple queue, which then contains both the IPv4 and the IPv6 address. Default: yes.

arguments.name: lease-time
arguments.description: Lease time for this client. When not set, or set to `0s`, the `lease-time` of the server is used.

arguments.name: always-broadcast
arguments.description: Whether to broadcast replies to this client even when it has not set the broadcast flag. Default: no.

arguments.name: dhcp-option
arguments.description: Options (`/ip/dhcp-server/option`) to send to this client. They take precedence over the options of the server and of the network.

arguments.name: dhcp-option-set
arguments.description: Option set (`/ip/dhcp-server/option/sets`) to send to this client. It takes precedence over the options of the server and of the network.

arguments.name: agent-circuit-id
arguments.description: When set, the lease matches requests whose relay agent information (option 82) contains this circuit ID, even if the MAC address or client ID differ.

arguments.name: agent-remote-id
arguments.description: When set, the lease matches requests whose relay agent information (option 82) contains this remote ID, even if the MAC address or client ID differ.

flags.name: R
flags.description: The lease was assigned by a RADIUS server.

flags.name: D
flags.description: The lease is dynamic: it was created when a client got an address from the pool. Use `make-static` to turn it into a static lease.

flags.name: B
flags.description: The client is blocked (`block-access=yes`) and gets no reply from the server.

readOnlyArguments.name: status
readOnlyArguments.type: enum (waiting | testing | declined | offered | bound | authorizing | conflict) { waiting:0, testing:1, declined:2, offered:3, bound:4, authorizing:5 }
readOnlyArguments.description:
State of the lease:
- `waiting` - A static lease that is not in use.
- `testing` - The server is checking the address for conflicts (`conflict-detection`).
- `offered` - The server offered the address and waits for the client's request.
- `bound` - The client uses the address.
- `authorizing` - The server waits for the reply from the RADIUS server.
- `conflict` - Another host already uses the address. The lease keeps the address out of use for the lease time; `check-status` frees it when the other host no longer answers.
- `declined` - The client declined the address with a DHCPDECLINE message.

readOnlyArguments.name: active-server

readOnlyArguments.name: active-agent-remote-id-ascii
readOnlyArguments.description: Remote ID from the relay agent information (option 82) of the client's request, as text.

readOnlyArguments.description: DHCP option 60 from last received DHCP request

readOnlyArguments.name: src-mac-address
readOnlyArguments.description: Source MAC address of the client's last request.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: Name of the matcher.

arguments.name: server

arguments.name: address-pool

arguments.name: option-set
arguments.description: Option set (`/ip/dhcp-server/option/sets`) to send to matching clients.

arguments.name: code
arguments.description: Code of the DHCP option to match (1-254).

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: Value to look for in the option, as text or as hex with the `0x` prefix.

arguments.name: matching-type
arguments.description:
How `value` is compared with the option:
- `exact` - The option must be equal to `value`.
- `substring` - `value` can appear anywhere in the option.
When two substring matchers match the same option, it is random which one applies.

arguments.name: address
arguments.description: Network this entry applies to, for example `192.168.88.0/24`.

arguments.name: gateway
arguments.description: Default gateway sent to clients (option 3). More than one gateway can be listed.

arguments.name: netmask
arguments.description: Subnet mask sent to clients, as a prefix length, when it should differ from the mask of `address`. With `0`, the mask of `address` is used.

arguments.name: dns-server
arguments.description: DNS servers sent to clients (option 6). When not set, the server sends the DNS servers the router itself uses (`/ip/dns`).

arguments.name: dns-none

arguments.name: wins-server
arguments.description: WINS servers sent to clients (option 44).

arguments.name: ntp-server
arguments.description: NTP servers sent to clients (option 42). When not set, the server sends the NTP servers the router itself uses.

arguments.name: ntp-none
arguments.description: Whether to send no NTP servers at all, not even those of the router. Default: no.

arguments.name: caps-manager
arguments.description: CAPsMAN addresses sent to clients (option 138).

arguments.name: domain
arguments.description: Domain name sent to clients (option 15).

arguments.name: next-server
arguments.description: Address of the server for the next step of network boot, sent in the `siaddr` field, for example a TFTP server. When not set, the address of the DHCP server is sent.

arguments.name: boot-file-name
arguments.description: Name of the boot file for network boot, sent in the `file` field.

arguments.name: dhcp-option
arguments.description: Options (`/ip/dhcp-server/option`) sent to clients in this network. Options of the server and of the lease take precedence.

arguments.name: dhcp-option-set
arguments.description: Option set (`/ip/dhcp-server/option/sets`) sent to clients in this network. Options of the server and of the lease take precedence.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: Name of the option, used where options are assigned.

arguments.name: code
arguments.description: DHCP option code (1-254).

arguments.name: value
arguments.description:
Value of the option. The value is converted according to how it is written:
- `'test'` - Text in quotes is sent as text (`74657374`).
- `'10.10.10.10'` - An IP address in quotes is sent as four bytes (`0a0a0a0a`).
- `s'10.10.10.10'` - With the `s` prefix, the value is always sent as text (`31302e31302e31302e3130`).
- `'10'` - A number in quotes is sent as one byte (`0a`).
- `0x0a0a` - A hex value is sent as it is.
Parts can be combined, for example `0x01'vards'$(HOSTNAME)`. These variables can be used:
- `$(HOSTNAME)` - The router's identity.
- `$(NETWORK_GATEWAY)` - The first gateway of the matching network (`/ip/dhcp-server/network`), filled in when the option is sent.
- `$(RADIUS_MT_STR1)`, `$(RADIUS_MT_STR2)` - MikroTik RADIUS attributes 24 and 25.
- `$(REMOTE_ID)` - Remote ID of the relay agent information (option 82).

arguments.name: file

File on the router with the names to block, as `/file/print` shows it. One name per line, in lower case, in one of these formats:
- `0.0.0.0 name`, `127.0.0.1 name` or `::1 name` - Hosts file format.
- `name` - Just the name.
Lines starting with `#` and comments after a name are ignored. Wildcards such as `*.example.com` and several names on one line are not supported.

arguments.name: url

arguments.name: ssl-verify

When the check fails, the router does not import the list and logs `http client error: SSL: ...` in the `dns` topic. For a server with a self-signed certificate, import its CA certificate or set `ssl-verify=no`. Default: yes.

readOnlyArguments.description: Domain name of the record.

readOnlyArguments.name: ttl
readOnlyArguments.description: Remaining time before the record expires from the cache. It counts down, and it is never longer than `cache-max-ttl` in [`/ip/dns`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/ip/dns/).

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: Name of the forwarder, used as `forward-to` in static `FWD` entries.

arguments.name: dns-servers
arguments.description: DNS servers of the forwarder, as IP addresses or DNS names, for example `dns-servers=1.1.1.1,8.8.8.8`.

arguments.name: doh-servers
arguments.description: DoH server URLs of the forwarder, for example `doh-servers=https://dns.google/dns-query`. The router looks up their host names through `servers` in `/ip/dns`.

arguments.name: verify-doh-cert
arguments.description: Whether the router verifies the certificates of the DoH servers against `/certificate` and the built-in trust store. A server with an untrusted certificate fails with `SSL: ssl: no trusted CA certificate found (6)` in the log. This default differs from `verify-doh-cert` in `/ip/dns`. Default: yes.

arguments.name: servers
arguments.description: Upstream DNS servers, IPv4 or IPv6 addresses, optionally with `@` to reach a server in another VRF. The router tries these servers before `dynamic-servers`, in the listed order. It waits `query-server-timeout` for an answer and then tries the next server. When a server answers, the router keeps using it for later queries.

arguments.name: use-doh-server
arguments.description: URL of a DNS over HTTPS (DoH) server, for example `https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query`. When it is set, the router sends every query over one reused HTTPS connection (TCP port 443) to this server, and `servers` and `dynamic-servers` are used only to look up the host name of the DoH server (A and AAAA over UDP port 53); a static entry for the host name also works. The router does not fall back to plain DNS: when the DoH server does not answer, clients get SERVFAIL after `query-total-timeout`, and the log shows `dns,error DoH server connection error: ...`, for example `Connection refused` or `timeout connecting`. Static `FWD` entries keep using their own servers over plain DNS. Only one DoH server can be set. ARM64 and x86 devices, including CHR, use HTTP/2; other architectures use HTTP/1.1, so DoH services that require HTTP/2, such as Quad9, work only on ARM64 and x86. Default: empty.

arguments.name: verify-doh-cert
arguments.description: Whether the router verifies the certificate of the DoH server against `/certificate` and the built-in trust store. Default: no.

arguments.name: doh-max-server-connections
arguments.description: Maximum number of HTTPS connections to the DoH server. Default: 5.

arguments.name: doh-max-concurrent-queries
arguments.description: Maximum number of DoH queries in progress at the same time. Default: 50.

arguments.name: doh-timeout
arguments.description: How long the router waits for an answer from the DoH server. Default: 5s.

arguments.name: allow-remote-requests
arguments.description: Whether the router answers DNS queries from other devices, on UDP and TCP port 53 of its addresses. With `no`, only the router itself uses the resolver. The default firewall drops connections from the WAN side; allow port 53 only from your own networks, so the router does not answer queries from the internet. Default: no.

arguments.name: max-udp-packet-size
arguments.description: Maximum size of a DNS message over UDP, in bytes. Default: 4096.

arguments.name: query-server-timeout
arguments.description: How long the router waits for an answer from one upstream server before it tries the next one. Default: 2s.

arguments.name: query-total-timeout
arguments.description: How long the router tries to resolve a query in total. When no server answers in this time, the client gets a SERVFAIL answer. Set it in relation to `query-server-timeout` and the number of servers. Default: 10s.

arguments.name: max-concurrent-queries
arguments.description: Largest number of queries that can wait for an upstream answer at the same time. While the limit is reached, the router drops new queries, also those it could answer from the cache, until a waiting query finishes. Default: 100.

arguments.name: max-concurrent-tcp-sessions
arguments.description: Maximum number of TCP connections from clients at the same time. Default: 20.

arguments.name: cache-size
arguments.description: Size of the DNS cache, in KiB. Adlist entries are kept in the cache too. Default: 2048.

arguments.name: cache-max-ttl
arguments.description: Longest time the router keeps an upstream answer in the cache. A longer TTL from the upstream server is shortened to this value, and clients get the remaining time. Static entries keep their own `ttl`. Default: 1w.

arguments.name: address-list-extra-time
arguments.description: Time added to the TTL of an answer before the router removes a dynamic address-list entry that a static entry with `address-list` created. Default: 0s.

arguments.name: vrf
arguments.description: VRF in which the resolver answers clients when `allow-remote-requests=yes`. Clients in other VRFs get no answer; the router's own lookups keep working. Upstream servers without a VRF suffix are reached through the main routing table; to reach a server in another VRF, write it as `address@vrf` in `servers`, for example `servers=10.0.0.1@vrf1,1.1.1.1`. Default: main.

arguments.name: mdns-repeat-ifaces
arguments.description: Interfaces between which the router repeats multicast DNS (mDNS). The router receives IPv4 mDNS packets (UDP port 5353 to 224.0.0.251) on each listed interface and sends them again from its own address on the other listed interfaces, so devices in different networks can discover each other. IPv6 mDNS (ff02::fb) is not repeated. The router handles the packets itself, so they pass the input chain of the firewall: input rules must not drop UDP port 5353 on these interfaces (the default firewall accepts it on `LAN` interfaces). Use interfaces that carry multicast, such as Ethernet, VLAN, bridge or EoIP interfaces; layer 3 tunnels such as WireGuard carry no multicast. Default: empty (no repeating).

readOnlyArguments.name: dynamic-servers
readOnlyArguments.description: DNS servers learned from other services, for example from the DHCP client with `use-peer-dns=yes`. The router tries them after `servers`.

readOnlyArguments.name: cache-used
readOnlyArguments.description: Part of `cache-size` in use, in KiB.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: Domain name of the entry. The router converts query names to lower case before matching, so the match is case-insensitive.

arguments.name: regexp
arguments.description: Regular expression the query name is matched against, instead of `name`. The router matches it against the name in lower case, so write the expression in lower case: an expression with capital letters never matches. The router creates no PTR record for regular expression entries. Do not let a regular expression overlap with other entries for the same names: the list order does not decide which of several matching entries answers. On the command line, write a backslash as `\\` and a `$` as `\$`; for example, `regexp="^host[0-9]+\\.example\\.com\$"` is stored as `^host[0-9]+\.example\.com$`. Check the stored value with `print`.

arguments.name: type
arguments.type: enum (NXDOMAIN | A | NS | CNAME | MX | TXT | AAAA | SRV | FWD) { NXDOMAIN:65281, A:1, NS:2, CNAME:5, MX:15, TXT:16, AAAA:28, SRV:33, FWD:65280 }
arguments.description:
Type of the entry.
- `A` (default) - IPv4 address in `address`.
- `AAAA` - IPv6 address in `address`.
- `CNAME` - Alias of the name in `cname`. The router answers with the CNAME record and the records of the target, from static entries or from upstream.
- `FWD` - Forward queries for the name to the server in `forward-to` instead of the upstream servers.
- `MX` - Mail server in `mx-exchange` with `mx-preference`.
- `NS` - Name server in `ns`.
- `NXDOMAIN` - Answer NXDOMAIN (the name does not exist) for every record type.
- `SRV` - Service location in `srv-target`, `srv-port`, `srv-priority` and `srv-weight`.
- `TXT` - Text in `text`.

arguments.name: forward-to
arguments.type:
alt { forwarder: enum
, ip: ipAddr
, ipv6: ip6Addr
, host: string
 }
arguments.description: Where the router forwards queries of a `FWD` entry: an IPv4 or IPv6 address or a DNS name of a server, or the name of a forwarder in [`/ip/dns/forwarders`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/ip/dns/forwarders). Without `forward-to`, the query goes to the normal servers (`servers`, `dynamic-servers` or the DoH server), and the name is exempt from adlists. When the server does not answer within `query-total-timeout`, the client gets a SERVFAIL answer.

arguments.name: address
arguments.description: IPv4 address of an `A` entry or IPv6 address of an `AAAA` entry. For entries with `name`, the router also answers reverse (PTR) queries for the address.

arguments.name: mx-preference
arguments.description: Preference of the mail server of an `MX` entry; lower values are preferred.

arguments.name: mx-exchange
arguments.description: Host name of the mail server of an `MX` entry.

arguments.name: cname
arguments.description: Target name of a `CNAME` entry.

arguments.name: text
arguments.description: Text of a `TXT` entry.

arguments.name: ns
arguments.description: Host name of the name server of an `NS` entry.

arguments.name: srv-priority
arguments.description: Priority of an `SRV` entry; lower values are preferred.

arguments.name: srv-weight
arguments.description: Weight of an `SRV` entry among entries with the same priority.

arguments.name: srv-port
arguments.description: TCP or UDP port of the service of an `SRV` entry.

arguments.name: srv-target
arguments.description: Host name that provides the service of an `SRV` entry.

arguments.name: ttl
arguments.description: Time to live in the answers for this entry. `cache-max-ttl` in [`/ip/dns`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/ip/dns/) does not shorten it. Default: 1d.

arguments.name: match-subdomain
arguments.description: Whether the entry also matches every name below `name`, at any depth. With `yes`, an entry for `example.com` also answers `www.example.com` and `a.b.example.com`. Default: no.

arguments.name: address-list
arguments.description: Firewall address list the router adds the answered addresses to, as dynamic entries with the comment `created for .`. For a `FWD` entry, these are the addresses in the upstream answer. The router removes an entry when the TTL of the answer and `address-list-extra-time` in [`/ip/dns`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/ip/dns/) have passed.

flags.name: D
flags.description: The entry was added by another service, not by a user.

flags.name: X
flags.description: The entry is disabled and the router ignores it. New entries are enabled.

arguments.name: list
arguments.description: Name of the address list. A new name creates the list. Rules match the list with `src-address-list` and `dst-address-list`.

arguments.name: address
arguments.description: An IP address, a prefix, a range or a DNS name. A prefix with host bits is stored as its network (`203.0.113.77/24` becomes `203.0.113.0/24`). A range that is exactly one prefix is stored as that prefix (`198.51.100.0-198.51.100.255` becomes `198.51.100.0/24`); other ranges stay ranges. Text that is not a valid address is stored as a DNS name without an error, so a short range such as `203.0.113.1-254` matches nothing; write ranges in full. For a DNS name, the router adds one dynamic entry for each A record in the answer, with the name as the comment, and resolves the name again when the record expires. An address that is already in the list is refused with `already have such entry`; overlapping entries are accepted.

arguments.name: timeout
arguments.description: Time after which the router removes the entry. An entry with a timeout is dynamic (`D`): it is not saved in the configuration or in exports, and a reboot clears it. The maximum is `35w3d13h13m56s`. Without a timeout, the entry stays until you remove it.

arguments.name: dynamic
arguments.description: With `yes`, the entry is dynamic (`D`) and has no timeout: it is not saved in the configuration and a reboot clears it. Default: no.

flags.name: X
flags.description: Disabled: the entry stays in the list but does not match.

flags.name: D
flags.description: Dynamic: the entry has a timeout or was added with `dynamic=yes`, by a firewall rule with a time or `none-dynamic`, from a resolved DNS name or by another feature (DNS, DHCP server). Dynamic entries are not saved in the configuration or in exports, and a reboot clears them.

readOnlyArguments.name: creation-time
readOnlyArguments.description: When the entry was created. A static entry keeps this time after a reboot; an imported entry gets the time of the import.

arguments.name: filter
arguments.description: Filter configuration for calea rules.

arguments.name: chain
arguments.type: enum (prerouting | input | forward | output | postrouting) { prerouting:1, input:2, forward:3, output:4, postrouting:5 }
arguments.description: Specifies to which chain the rule will be added. If the input does not match the name of an already defined chain, a new chain will be created.

arguments.name: action
arguments.description:
Action to take if a packet is matched by the rule:
- `sniff` - sniff the packet.
- `sniff-pc` - sniff the packet and send it to the specified Packet Capturer target.

arguments.name: sniff-target
arguments.description: IP address to send the sniffed packet to.

arguments.name: sniff-target-port
arguments.description: Port to send the sniffed packet to.

arguments.name: sniff-id
arguments.description: ID of the sniffing session.

arguments.name: tls-host
arguments.description: Matches HTTPS traffic based on TLS SNI hostname. Accepts GLOB syntax for wildcard matching. The matcher will not be able to match the hostname if the TLS handshake frame is fragmented into multiple TCP segments.

arguments.name: connection-limit
arguments.description: Matches connections per address or address block after a given value is reached. You should use this together with `connection-state=new` and/or with `tcp-flags=syn` because the matcher is very resource-intensive.

arguments.name: layer7-protocol
arguments.description: Layer7 filter name defined in the layer7 protocol menu.

arguments.name: realm
arguments.description: Matches the routing realm. IPv4 only.

arguments.name: protocol
arguments.description: Matches the particular IP protocol specified by protocol name or number.

arguments.name: src-address
arguments.description: Matches packets whose source is equal to the specified IP or falls into the specified IP range.

arguments.name: dst-address
arguments.description: Matches packets whose destination is equal to the specified IP or falls into the specified IP range.

arguments.name: fragment
arguments.description: Matches fragmented packets. The first (starting) fragment does not count. If connection tracking is enabled there will be no fragments as the system automatically assembles every packet. IPv4 only.

arguments.name: psd
arguments.description:
Attempts to detect TCP and UDP scans. Parameters are in the following format: `WeightThreshold, DelayThreshold, LowPortWeight, HighPortWeight`.
- `WeightThreshold` - total weight of the latest TCP/UDP packets with different destination ports coming from the same host to be treated as port scan sequence.
- `DelayThreshold` - delay for the packets with different destination ports coming from the same host to be treated as possible port scan subsequence.
- `LowPortWeight` - the weight of the packets with privileged destination port (<1024).
- `HighPortWeight` - the weight of the packets with a non-privileged destination port. IPv4 only.

arguments.name: ipv4-options
arguments.type:
super { options: enum (strict-source-routing | loose-source-routing | no-source-routing | record-route | no-record-route | timestamp | no-timestamp | router-alert | no-router-alert | any | none) { strict-source-routing:0x1, loose-source-routing:0x2, no-source-routing:0x4, record-route:0x8, no-record-route:0x10, timestamp:0x20, no-timestamp:0x40, router-alert:0x80, no-router-alert:0x100, any:0x200, none:0x400 }
 }
arguments.description:
Matches IPv4 header options.
- `any` - matches packets with at least one of the IPv4 options.
- `loose-source-routing` - matches packets with a loose source routing option.
- `no-record-route` - matches packets with no record route option.
- `no-router-alert` - matches packets with no router alert option.
- `no-source-routing` - matches packets with no source routing option.
- `no-timestamp` - matches packets with no timestamp option.
- `record-route` - matches packets with record route option.
- `router-alert` - matches packets with router alert option.
- `strict-source-routing` - matches packets with a strict source routing option.
- `timestamp` - matches packets with a timestamp. IPv4 only.

arguments.name: src-address-type
arguments.description:
Matches the source address type:
- `unicast` - an IP address used for point-to-point transmission.
- `local` - the address is assigned to one of the router's interfaces.
- `broadcast` - a packet is sent to all devices in the subnet.
- `multicast` - a packet is forwarded to a defined group of devices.

arguments.name: dst-address-type
arguments.description:
Matches the destination address type:
- `unicast` - an IP address used for point-to-point transmission.
- `local` - the destination address is assigned to one of the router's interfaces.
- `broadcast` - a packet is sent to all devices in a subnet.
- `multicast` - a packet is forwarded to a defined group of devices.

arguments.name: src-address-list
arguments.description: Matches the source address of a packet against a user-defined address list. Supports only one list.

arguments.name: dst-address-list
arguments.description: Matches the destination address of a packet against a user-defined address list. Supports only one list.

arguments.name: hotspot
arguments.description:
Matches packets received from HotSpot clients against various HotSpot matchers.
- `auth` - matches authenticated HotSpot client packets.
- `from-client` - matches packets coming from the HotSpot client.
- `http` - matches HTTP requests sent to the HotSpot server.
- `local-dst` - matches packets destined to the HotSpot server.
- `to-client` - matches packets sent to the HotSpot client. IPv4 only.

arguments.name: address-list
arguments.description: Name of the address list to be used. Applicable if the action is `add-dst-to-address-list` or `add-src-to-address-list`.

arguments.name: address-list-timeout
arguments.description:
Time interval after which the address will be removed from the address list specified by the `address-list` parameter. Used in conjunction with `add-dst-to-address-list` or `add-src-to-address-list` actions.
- `none-dynamic` (`00:00:00`) will leave the address in the address list till reboot.
- `none-static` will leave the address in the address list forever and will be included in the configuration export/backup.

arguments.name: ttl
arguments.description: Matches the packet TTL value. IPv4 only.

arguments.name: connection-mark
arguments.description: Matches packets marked by the mangle facility with a particular connection mark. If `no-mark` is set, the rule will match any unmarked connection.

arguments.name: connection-type
arguments.description: Matches packets from related connections based on information from their connection tracking helpers. A relevant connection helper must be enabled under `/ip/firewall/service-port`.

arguments.name: connection-bytes
arguments.description: Matches packets only if a given amount of bytes has been transferred through the particular connection. 0 means infinity, for example `connection-bytes=2000000-0` means that the rule matches if more than 2MB has been transferred through the relevant connection.

arguments.name: connection-rate
arguments.description: Allows capturing traffic based on the present speed of the connection.

arguments.name: routing-mark
arguments.description: Matches packets marked by the mangle facility with a particular routing mark.

arguments.name: in-interface
arguments.description: Interface the packet has entered the router.

arguments.name: out-interface
arguments.description: Interface the packet is leaving the router.

arguments.name: in-interface-list
arguments.description: Set of interfaces defined in interface list. Works the same as `in-interface`.

arguments.name: out-interface-list
arguments.description: Set of interfaces defined in interface list. Works the same as `out-interface`.

arguments.name: in-bridge-port
arguments.description: Actual interface the packet has entered the router if the incoming interface is a bridge. Works only if `use-ip-firewall` is enabled in bridge settings.

arguments.name: out-bridge-port
arguments.description: Actual interface the packet leaves the router if the outgoing interface is a bridge. Works only if `use-ip-firewall` is enabled in bridge settings.

arguments.name: in-bridge-port-list
arguments.description: Set of interfaces defined in interface list. Works the same as `in-bridge-port`.

arguments.name: out-bridge-port-list
arguments.description: Set of interfaces defined in interface list. Works the same as `out-bridge-port`.

arguments.name: packet-mark
arguments.description: Matches packets marked by the mangle facility with a particular packet mark. If `no-mark` is set, the rule will match any unmarked packet.

arguments.name: src-port
arguments.description: List of source ports and ranges of source ports. Applicable only if the protocol is TCP or UDP.

arguments.name: dst-port
arguments.description: List of destination port numbers or port number ranges.

arguments.name: port
arguments.description: Matches if any (source or destination) port matches the specified list of ports or port ranges. Applicable only if `protocol` is TCP or UDP.

arguments.name: icmp-options
arguments.description: Matches ICMP type:code fields.

arguments.name: src-mac-address
arguments.description: Matches the source MAC address of the packet.

arguments.name: content
arguments.description: Matches packets that contain the specified text.

arguments.name: ingress-priority
arguments.description: Matches the priority of an ingress packet. Priority may be derived from VLAN, WMM, DSCP, or MPLS EXP bit.

arguments.name: priority
arguments.description: Matches the packet's priority after a new priority has been set. Priority may be derived from VLAN, WMM, DSCP, MPLS EXP bit, or from the priority set by using the set-priority action.

arguments.name: dscp
arguments.description: Matches the DSCP IP header field.

arguments.name: limit
arguments.type:
super { !
, count: num [1 .. 32000000000]
, [time] [ /time [1 .. ]]
, [burst] ,num [ .. 2000000000]

arguments.name: action
arguments.type: enum (accept | jump | return | log | passthrough | add-src-to-address-list | add-dst-to-address-list | drop | reject | tarpit | fasttrack-connection) { accept:0, jump:1, return:2, log:3, passthrough:4, add-src-to-address-list:5, add-dst-to-address-list:6, drop:10, reject:11, tarpit:12, fasttrack-connection:40 }
arguments.description:
Action to take if a packet is matched by the rule:
- `accept` - accept the packet. A packet is not passed to the next firewall rule.
- `add-dst-to-address-list` - add the destination address to the address list specified by the `address-list` parameter.
- `add-src-to-address-list` - add the source address to the address list specified by the `address-list` parameter.
- `jump` - jump to the user-defined chain specified by the value of the `jump-target` parameter.
- `log` - add a message to the system log containing the following data: in-interface, out-interface, src-mac, protocol, src-ip:port->dst-ip:port, and length of the packet. After a packet is matched it is passed to the next rule in the list, similar to `passthrough`.
- `passthrough` - if a packet is matched by the rule, increase the counter and go to the next rule (useful for statistics).
- `return` - passes control back to the chain from where the jump took place.
- `drop` - drop the packet.
- `reject` - reject the packet and send an ICMP response.
- `tarpit` - capture and hold the connection open.
- `fasttrack-connection` - fasttrack the connection.

arguments.name: jump-target
arguments.description: Name of the target chain to jump to. Applicable only if `action=jump`.

arguments.name: reject-with
arguments.type: enum (icmp-network-unreachable | icmp-host-unreachable | icmp-protocol-unreachable | icmp-port-unreachable | icmp-net-prohibited | icmp-host-prohibited | tcp-reset | icmp-admin-prohibited) { icmp-network-unreachable:0, icmp-host-unreachable:1, icmp-protocol-unreachable:2, icmp-port-unreachable:3, icmp-net-prohibited:5, icmp-host-prohibited:6, tcp-reset:7, icmp-admin-prohibited:8 }
arguments.description:
Specifies the [ICMP error](https://www.iana.org/assignments/icmp-parameters/icmp-parameters.xhtml) to be sent back if the packet is rejected. Applicable if `action=reject`.
- `icmp-network-unreachable` - sends an ICMP port unreachable message. ICMP type 3, code 0
- `icmp-host-unreachable` - sends an ICMP port unreachable message. ICMP type 3, code 1
- `icmp-protocol-unreachable` - sends an ICMP port unreachable message. ICMP type 3, code 2
- `icmp-port-unreachable` - sends an ICMP port unreachable message. ICMP type 3, code 3
- `icmp-net-prohibited` - sends an ICMP address prohibited message. ICMP type 3, code 9
- `icmp-host-prohibited` - sends an ICMP address prohibited message. ICMP type 3, code 10
- `tcp-reset` - sends a TCP segment with the RST flag set.
- `icmp-admin-prohibited` - sends an ICMP address prohibited message. ICMP type 3, code 13

arguments.name: hw-offload
arguments.description: Enables or disables [FastTrack hardware offloading](/docs/7.25/bridging-and-switching/l3-hardware-offloading#offloading-fasttrack-connections). Supported only on [switches with FastTrack offloading](/docs/7.25/bridging-and-switching/l3-hardware-offloading) and when `action=fasttrack-connection` is set.

arguments.name: tcp-flags
arguments.description:
Matches the specified TCP flags:
- `ack` - acknowledging data.
- `cwr` - congestion window reduced.
- `ece` - ECN-echo flag (explicit congestion notification).
- `fin` - close connection.
- `psh` - push function.
- `rst` - reset connection.
- `syn` - new connection.
- `urg` - urgent data.

arguments.name: p2p
arguments.description: Matches some unencrypted P2P protocols. Deprecated since mostly everything is encrypted and requires deep packet inspection to identify. IPv4 only.

arguments.name: connection-state
arguments.description:
Interprets the connection tracking analytics data for a particular packet:
- `established` - a packet that belongs to an existing connection.
- `invalid` - a packet that does not have a determined state in connection tracking (usually severe out-of-order packets, packets with wrong sequence/ack number, or in case of resource over usage on the router). An invalid packet will not participate in NAT (as only connection-state=new packets do), and will still contain the original source IP address when routed. You should drop all `connection-state=invalid` packets in the firewall filter forward and input chains.
- `new` - the packet has started a new connection or is otherwise associated with a connection that has not seen packets in both directions.
- `related` - a packet that is related to, but not part of an existing connection, such as ICMP errors or a packet that begins an FTP data connection.
- `untracked` - a packet that was set to bypass connection tracking in firewall RAW tables.

arguments.name: connection-nat-state
arguments.description:
Matches connections that are source-natted, destination-natted, or both. The `connection-state=related` connections' connection-nat-state is determined by the direction of the first packet, and if connection tracking needs to use dst-nat to deliver this connection to the same hosts as the main connection, it will be in connection-nat-state=dstnat even if there are no dst-nat rules at all.
`ein-snat` and `ein-dnat` are source and destination nated connections when endpoint-independent NAT is used.

arguments.name: tls-host
arguments.description: Matches HTTPS traffic based on TLS SNI hostname. Accepts GLOB syntax for wildcard matching. The matcher will not be able to match the hostname if the TLS handshake frame is fragmented into multiple TCP segments.

arguments.name: connection-limit
arguments.description: Matches connections per address or address block after a given value is reached. You should use this together with `connection-state=new` and/or with `tcp-flags=syn` because the matcher is very resource-intensive.

arguments.name: layer7-protocol
arguments.description: Layer7 filter name defined in the layer7 protocol menu.

arguments.name: realm
arguments.description: Matches the routing realm. IPv4 only.

arguments.name: protocol
arguments.description: Matches the particular IP protocol specified by protocol name or number.

arguments.name: src-address
arguments.description: Matches packets whose source is equal to the specified IP or falls into the specified IP range.

arguments.name: dst-address
arguments.description: Matches packets whose destination is equal to the specified IP or falls into the specified IP range.

arguments.name: fragment
arguments.description: Matches fragmented packets. The first (starting) fragment does not count. If connection tracking is enabled there will be no fragments as the system automatically assembles every packet. IPv4 only.

arguments.name: psd
arguments.description:
Attempts to detect TCP and UDP scans. Parameters are in the following format: `WeightThreshold, DelayThreshold, LowPortWeight, HighPortWeight`.
- `WeightThreshold` - total weight of the latest TCP/UDP packets with different destination ports coming from the same host to be treated as port scan sequence.
- `DelayThreshold` - delay for the packets with different destination ports coming from the same host to be treated as possible port scan subsequence.
- `LowPortWeight` - the weight of the packets with privileged destination port (<1024).
- `HighPortWeight` - the weight of the packets with a non-privileged destination port. IPv4 only.

super { options: enum (strict-source-routing | loose-source-routing | no-source-routing | record-route | no-record-route | timestamp | no-timestamp | router-alert | no-router-alert | any | none) { strict-source-routing:0x1, loose-source-routing:0x2, no-source-routing:0x4, record-route:0x8, no-record-route:0x10, timestamp:0x20, no-timestamp:0x40, router-alert:0x80, no-router-alert:0x100, any:0x200, none:0x400 }

arguments.name: address-list-timeout
arguments.description:
How long the address stays in `address-list` after the `add-src-to-address-list` or `add-dst-to-address-list` action adds it. With a time, the rule adds a dynamic entry (`D`) that the router removes when the time ends; each new match of the rule resets the time to its full value. The maximum is `35w3d13h13m56s`. - `none-static` - Add a static entry. It is saved in the configuration and in exports, and stays after a reboot until you remove it.

arguments.name: action
arguments.type: enum (accept | jump | return | log | passthrough | add-src-to-address-list | add-dst-to-address-list | sniff-tzsp | sniff-pc | drop | mark-packet | mark-connection | change-mss | change-dscp | strip-ipv4-options | change-ttl | mark-routing | set-priority | clear-df | fasttrack-connection | route) { accept:0, jump:1, return:2, log:3, passthrough:4, add-src-to-address-list:5, add-dst-to-address-list:6, sniff-tzsp:7, sniff-pc:8, drop:10, mark-packet:30, mark-connection:31, change-mss:32, change-dscp:33, strip-ipv4-options:34, change-ttl:35, mark-routing:36, set-priority:37, clear-df:39, fasttrack-connection:40, route:41 }
arguments.description:
Action to take if a packet is matched by the rule:
- `accept` - accept the packet. A packet is not passed to the next firewall rule.
- `add-dst-to-address-list` - add the destination address to the address list specified by the `address-list` parameter.
- `add-src-to-address-list` - add the source address to the address list specified by the `address-list` parameter.
- `jump` - jump to the user-defined chain specified by the value of the `jump-target` parameter.
- `log` - add a message to the system log containing the following data: in-interface, out-interface, src-mac, protocol, src-ip:port->dst-ip:port, and length of the packet. After a packet is matched it is passed to the next rule in the list, similar to `passthrough`.
- `passthrough` - if a packet is matched by the rule, increase the counter and go to the next rule (useful for statistics).
- `return` - passes control back to the chain from where the jump took place.
- `sniff-tzsp` - send a packet to a remote TZSP compatible system (such as Wireshark). Set remote target with `sniff-target` and `sniff-target-port` parameters (Wireshark recommends port 37008). After a packet is matched it is passed to the next rule in the list, similar to `passthrough`.
- `sniff-pc` - send a packet to a remote RouterOS CALEA server. After a packet is matched it is passed to the next rule in the list, similar to `passthrough`.
- `drop` - silently drop the packet.
- `mark-packet` - mark the packet with the specified `new-packet-mark`.
- `mark-connection` - mark the connection with the specified `new-connection-mark`.
- `change-mss` - change the Maximum Segment Size field value of the packet to a value specified by the `new-mss` parameter.
- `change-dscp` - change the Differentiated Services Code Point (DSCP) field value specified by the `new-dscp` parameter.
- `change-ttl` - change the Time to Live field value of the packet to a value specified by the `new-ttl` parameter.
- `mark-routing` - place a mark specified by the `new-routing-mark` parameter on a packet. This kind of mark is used for policy routing purposes only. Do not apply any other routing marks besides `main` for packets processed by FastTrack, since FastTrack can only work in the main routing table.
- `set-priority` - set the priority of the packet.
- `clear-df` - clear the Don't Fragment flag.
- `fasttrack-connection` - mark the connection for FastTrack. After a packet is matched it is passed to the next rule in the list, similar to `passthrough`.
- `route` - forces packets to a gateway IP specified by 'route-dst' parameter, by ignoring normal routing decisions (prerouting chain only).
- `strip-ipv4-options` - strip IPv4 option fields from IP header. The action does not actually remove IPv4 options but rather replaces all option octets with NOP. Further matcher with `ipv4-options=any` will still match the packet.

arguments.name: new-mss
arguments.description: Sets a new MSS for a packet. **Important:** Clamp-to-pmtu feature sets the DF bit in the IP header to dynamically discover the PMTU of a path. The host sends all datagrams on that path with the DF bit set until it receives ICMP Destination Unreachable messages with a code meaning "fragmentation needed and DF set". Upon receipt of such a message, the source host reduces its assumed PMTU for the path.

arguments.name: new-dscp

arguments.name: new-priority

arguments.name: passthrough

arguments.name: tcp-flags
arguments.description:
Matches the specified TCP flags:
- `ack` - acknowledging data.
- `cwr` - congestion window reduced.
- `ece` - ECN-echo flag (explicit congestion notification).
- `fin` - close connection.
- `psh` - push function.
- `rst` - reset connection.
- `syn` - new connection.
- `urg` - urgent data.

arguments.name: p2p
arguments.description: Matches some unencrypted P2P protocols. Deprecated since mostly everything is encrypted and requires deep packet inspection to identify. IPv4 only.

arguments.name: connection-state
arguments.description:
Interprets the connection tracking analytics data for a particular packet:
 - `established` - a packet that belongs to an existing connection.
 - `invalid` - a packet that does not have a determined state in connection tracking (usually severe out-of-order packets, packets with wrong sequence/ack number, or in case of resource over usage on the router). An invalid packet will not participate in NAT (as only connection-state=new packets do), and will still contain the original source IP address when routed. You should drop all `connection-state=invalid` packets in the firewall filter forward and input chains.
 - `new` - the packet has started a new connection or is otherwise associated with a connection that has not seen packets in both directions.
 - `related` - a packet that is related to, but not part of an existing connection, such as ICMP errors or a packet that begins an FTP data connection.
 - `untracked` - a packet that was set to bypass connection tracking in firewall RAW tables.

arguments.name: connection-nat-state
arguments.description:
Matches connections that are source-natted, destination-natted, or both. The `connection-state=related` connections' connection-nat-state is determined by the direction of the first packet, and if connection tracking needs to use dst-nat to deliver this connection to the same hosts as the main connection, it will be in connection-nat-state=dstnat even if there are no dst-nat rules at all.
`ein-snat` and `ein-dnat` are source and destination nated connections when endpoint-independent NAT is used.

arguments.name: limit
arguments.type:
super { !
, count: num [1 .. 32000000000]
, [time] [ /time [1 .. ]]
, [burst] ,num [ .. 2000000000]
, [mode] [ :enum (packet | bit) { packet:0, bit:1 }]
 }
arguments.description:
Matches packets up to a limited rate (packet rate or bit rate). A rule with this matcher will match until this limit is reached. Parameters are written in the following format: `rate[/time],burst:mode`.
- `rate` - packet or bit count per time interval to match.
- `time` - specifies the time interval in which the packet or bit rate cannot be exceeded (optional, 1s will be used if not specified).
- `burst` - initial number of packets or bits to match: this number gets recharged every 10ms so burst should be at least 1/100 of a rate per second.
- `mode` - packet or bit mode.

arguments.name: dst-limit
arguments.description:
Matches packets until a given rate is exceeded. Rate is defined as packets per time interval. As opposed to the `limit` matcher, every flow has its own limit. Flow is defined by a mode parameter. Parameters are written in the following format: `rate[/time],burst,mode[/expire]`.
- `rate` - packet count per time interval per-flow to match.
- `time` - specifies the time interval in which the packet count rate per flow cannot be exceeded (optional, 1s will be used if not specified).
- `burst` - initial number of packets per flow to match: this number gets recharged by one every time/rate, up to this number.
- `mode` - specifies what unique fields define flow (src-address, dst-address, src-and-dst-address, dst-address-and-port, addresses-and-dst-port).
- `expire` - specifies interval after which flow with no packets will be allowed to be deleted (optional).

arguments.name: time
arguments.type:
super { !
, start: time [0 .. 86400]
, [end] -time [0 .. 86400]
, [day] ,ubit (sun, mon, tue, wed, thu, fri, sat)
 }
arguments.description: Creates a filter based on the packets' arrival time and date or, for locally generated packets, departure time and date. The matcher takes into account the time and timezone configured on the router.

arguments.name: random

arguments.name: nth
arguments.description: Matches every nth packet: `nth=2,1` will match every first packet of 2, hence, 50% of all the traffic matched by the rule.

arguments.name: per-connection-classifier
arguments.description: PCC matcher allows dividing traffic into equal streams with the ability to keep packets with a specific set of options in one particular stream.

arguments.name: packet-size

arguments.name: log

arguments.name: log-prefix
arguments.description: Adds the specified text at the beginning of every log message. Applicable if `action=log` or `log=yes` is configured.

arguments.name: ipsec-policy
arguments.description:
Matches the policy used by IPsec. Value is written in the following format: `direction, policy`.
- `in` - valid in the PREROUTING, INPUT, and FORWARD chains.
- `out` - valid in the POSTROUTING, OUTPUT, and FORWARD chains.
- `ipsec` - matches if the packet is subject to IPsec processing.
- `none` - matches packets that are not subject to IPsec processing.

arguments.name: chain
arguments.description: Specifies to which chain the rule will be added. If the input does not match the name of an already defined chain, a new chain will be created.

arguments.name: action
arguments.type: enum (accept | jump | return | log | passthrough | add-src-to-address-list | add-dst-to-address-list | src-nat | masquerade | dst-nat | redirect | same | netmap | endpoint-independent-nat | socksify) { accept:0, jump:1, return:2, log:3, passthrough:4, add-src-to-address-list:5, add-dst-to-address-list:6, src-nat:20, masquerade:21, dst-nat:22, redirect:23, same:24, netmap:25, endpoint-independent-nat:26, socksify:27 }
arguments.description:
Action to take if a packet is matched by the rule:
- `accept` - accept the packet. A packet is not passed to the next firewall rule.
- `add-dst-to-address-list` - add the destination address to the address list specified by the `address-list` parameter.
- `add-src-to-address-list` - add the source address to the address list specified by the `address-list` parameter.
- `jump` - jump to the user-defined chain specified by the value of the `jump-target` parameter.
- `log` - add a message to the system log containing the following data: in-interface, out-interface, src-mac, protocol, src-ip:port->dst-ip:port, and length of the packet. After a packet is matched it is passed to the next rule in the list, similar to `passthrough`.
- `passthrough` - if a packet is matched by the rule, increase the counter and go to the next rule (useful for statistics).
- `return` - passes control back to the chain from where the jump took place.
- `src-nat` - replaces the source address of an IP packet with values specified by `to-addresses` and `to-ports` parameters.
- `masquerade` - replaces the source port of an IP packet with one specified by `to-ports` parameter and replaces the source address of an IP packet with the IP determined by the routing facility.
- `dst-nat` - replaces the destination address and/or port of an IP packet with values specified by `to-addresses` and `to-ports` parameters.
- `redirect` - replaces the destination port of an IP packet with one specified by `to-ports` parameter and destination address to the address of the virtual or physical incoming interface (interface that received the packet).
- `same` - gives a particular client the same source/destination IP address from a supplied range for each connection. This is most frequently used for services that expect the same client address for multiple connections from the same client.
- `netmap` - creates a static 1:1 mapping of one set of IP addresses to another one. Often used to distribute public IP addresses to hosts on private networks.
- `endpoint-independent-nat` - uses endpoint-independent mapping and filtering. Works only with UDP protocol.
- `socksify` - routes traffic specified by firewall rules through SOCKS proxy server. Requires `socks5-server` and `socks5-port` parameters or `socksify-service` parameter. [relevant socksify information](/docs/7.25/network-management/socks/socksify)

Matches packets until a given rate is exceeded. Rate is defined as packets per time interval. As opposed to the `limit` matcher, every flow has its own limit. Flow is defined by a mode parameter. Parameters are written in the following format: `rate[/time],burst,mode[/expire]`.
- `rate` - packet count per time interval per-flow to match.
- `time` - specifies the time interval in which the packet count rate per flow cannot be exceeded (optional, 1s will be used if not specified).
- `burst` - initial number of packets per flow to match: this number gets recharged by one every time/rate, up to this number.
- `mode` - specifies what unique fields define flow (src-address, dst-address, src-and-dst-address, dst-address-and-port, addresses-and-dst-port).
- `expire` - specifies interval after which flow with no packets will be allowed to be deleted (optional).

arguments.name: ipsec-policy
arguments.description:
Matches the policy used by IPsec. Value is written in the following format: `direction, policy`.
- `in` - valid in the PREROUTING, INPUT, and FORWARD chains.
- `out` - valid in the POSTROUTING, OUTPUT, and FORWARD chains.

arguments.name: action
arguments.type: enum (accept | jump | return | log | passthrough | add-src-to-address-list | add-dst-to-address-list | drop | notrack) { accept:0, jump:1, return:2, log:3, passthrough:4, add-src-to-address-list:5, add-dst-to-address-list:6, drop:10, notrack:42 }
arguments.description:
Action to take if a packet is matched by the rule:
- `accept` - accept the packet. A packet is not passed to the next firewall rule.
- `add-dst-to-address-list` - add the destination address to the address list specified by the `address-list` parameter.
- `add-src-to-address-list` - add the source address to the address list specified by the `address-list` parameter.
- `jump` - jump to the user-defined chain specified by the value of the `jump-target` parameter.
- `log` - add a message to the system log containing the following data: in-interface, out-interface, src-mac, protocol, src-ip:port->dst-ip:port, and length of the packet. After a packet is matched it is passed to the next rule in the list, similar to `passthrough`.
- `passthrough` - if a packet is matched by the rule, increase the counter and go to the next rule (useful for statistics).
- `return` - passes control back to the chain from where the jump took place.
- `drop` - drop the packet.
- `notrack` - do not send a packet to connection tracking. Useful when you still need to use regular firewall, but do not require connection tracking.

arguments.name: jump-target
arguments.description: Name of the target chain to jump to. Applicable only if `action=jump`.

- `fin` - close connection.
- `psh` - push function.
- `rst` - reset connection.
- `syn` - new connection.
- `urg` - urgent data.

- `mode` - packet or bit mode.

arguments.name: address-list-timeout
arguments.description:
How long the address stays in `address-list` after the `add-src-to-address-list` or `add-dst-to-address-list` action adds it. With a time, the rule adds a dynamic entry (`D`) that the router removes when the time ends; each new match of the rule resets the time to its full value. The maximum is `35w3d13h13m56s`. An address that is already a static entry in the list stays static.
- `none-dynamic` (`0s`) - Add a dynamic entry without a timeout. It is not saved in the configuration and a reboot clears it.
- `none-static` - Add a static entry. It is saved in the configuration and in exports, and stays after a reboot until you remove it.

arguments.name: interface
arguments.description: Interface on which to aggregate or compress outgoing packets and unpack incoming ones. The router packs only toward a neighbor that announces unpacking through neighbor discovery, so discovery must run on this interface on both routers. Both routers must be configured symmetrically.

arguments.name: packing
arguments.type: enum (none | simple | compress-headers | compress-all) { none:0x00, simple:0x01, compress-headers:0x03, compress-all:0x07 }
arguments.description:
Action to perform on outgoing packets:
- `none` (default) - Send packets as they are.
- `simple` - Aggregate packets only.
- `compress-headers` - Aggregate packets and compress their headers; leave the payload unchanged.
- `compress-all` - Aggregate packets and compress headers and payload.

arguments.name: unpacking
arguments.type: enum (none | simple | compress-headers | compress-all) { none:0x00, simple:0x01, compress-headers:0x03, compress-all:0x07 }
arguments.description:
Action to perform on incoming packets. The router announces this setting to its neighbors (the `unpack` field in `/ip/neighbor`):
- `none` (default) - Do nothing with received packets.
- `simple` - Unpack aggregated packets.
- `compress-headers` - Unpack aggregated packets and decompress headers.
- `compress-all` - Unpack aggregated packets and decompress headers and payload.

arguments.name: aggregated-size
arguments.description: Size in bytes that packing tries to reach before it sends an aggregated packet. Packing waits to fill packets, so it adds delay on the link. Range: 20..16384. Default: 1500.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: Name of the pool.

arguments.name: ranges
arguments.description: IP address list of non-overlapping IP address ranges in the form of: `from1-to1,from2-to2,...,fromN-toN`. For example, `10.0.0.1-10.0.0.27,10.0.0.32-10.0.0.47`.

arguments.name: next-pool
arguments.description: When IP address acquisition is performed from a pool that has no free addresses, and the next-pool property is set, then an IP address will be acquired from the next pool.

arguments.name: pool
