arguments.name: src-address
arguments.description: Address of the client: an IPv4 address, range or prefix, or an IPv6 prefix.

arguments.name: dst-address
arguments.description: Address of the server the proxy connects to, which is the resolved address of the host name in the request. Same format as `src-address`.

arguments.name: dst-port
arguments.description: Port of the server, for HTTPS requests the port of the `CONNECT` tunnel. A port, a range or a comma-separated list, for example `dst-port=!443`.

arguments.name: local-port
arguments.description: Port of the proxy the request arrived on. Use it when `port` in [`/ip/proxy`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/ip/proxy/) lists several ports.

arguments.name: dst-host
arguments.description:
Host name of the request, for HTTPS requests the host of the `CONNECT` tunnel. The value must match the whole name and is not case-sensitive, so `example.com` does not match `www.example.com`.
- Wildcards: `*` matches any characters and `?` one character, for example `*.example.com`.
- A value that starts with `:` is a regular expression, which can match any part of the name: `:mail` matches `mail.example.com`. Anchor it with `^` and `$`, for example `:^www`.

arguments.name: path
arguments.description:
Path of the requested URL, including the query string, for example `/music/a.mp3?x=1`. Wildcards and regular expressions work as in `dst-host`.
- Wildcards must match the whole path including the query string, so `*.mp3` matches `/music/a.mp3` but not `/music/a.mp3?x=1`.
- The path always starts with `/`, so the router refuses a value such as `music/*`, which could never match.
- HTTPS requests have no path, so a rule with `path` never matches them.

arguments.name: method
arguments.description: HTTP method of the request: `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `CONNECT`, `OPTIONS`, `DELETE` or `TRACE`. Clients of the proxy request HTTPS pages with `CONNECT`. The methods are defined in [RFC 9110](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#name-methods).

arguments.name: action
arguments.description:
What the proxy does with a matching request.
- `allow` (default) - Pass the request on.
- `deny` - Answer with an HTTP 403 error page.
- `redirect` - Answer with HTTP 307 and the URL in `action-data` as the new location.
- `url-append` - Add the text in `action-data` to the end of the requested URL, after the path and query string, and pass the request on.

arguments.name: action-data
arguments.description: redirect URL/append URL. With `action=redirect`, the URL the client is sent to, for example `http://intranet.example.com/blocked.html`. With `action=url-append`, the text added to the end of the requested URL, as it is, without a separator.

flags.name: X
flags.description: disabled. The rule is not used. New rules are created enabled.

arguments.name: src-address
arguments.description: Address of the client: an IPv4 address, range or prefix, or an IPv6 prefix.

arguments.name: dst-address
arguments.description: Address of the server the proxy connects to, which is the resolved address of the host name in the request. Same format as `src-address`.

arguments.name: dst-port
arguments.description: Port of the server, for HTTPS requests the port of the `CONNECT` tunnel. A port, a range or a comma-separated list, for example `dst-port=!443`.

arguments.name: local-port
arguments.description: Port of the proxy the request arrived on. Use it when `port` in [`/ip/proxy`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/ip/proxy/) lists several ports.

arguments.name: dst-host
arguments.description:
Host name of the request, for HTTPS requests the host of the `CONNECT` tunnel. The value must match the whole name and is not case-sensitive, so `example.com` does not match `www.example.com`.
- Wildcards: `*` matches any characters and `?` one character, for example `*.example.com`.
- A value that starts with `:` is a regular expression, which can match any part of the name: `:mail` matches `mail.example.com`. Anchor it with `^` and `$`, for example `:^www`.

arguments.name: path
arguments.description:
Path of the requested URL, including the query string, for example `/music/a.mp3?x=1`. Wildcards and regular expressions work as in `dst-host`.
- Wildcards must match the whole path including the query string, so `*.mp3` matches `/music/a.mp3` but not `/music/a.mp3?x=1`.
- The path always starts with `/`, so the router refuses a value such as `music/*`, which could never match.
- HTTPS requests have no path, so a rule with `path` never matches them.

arguments.name: method
arguments.description: HTTP method of the request: `GET`, `HEAD`, `POST`, `PUT`, `CONNECT`, `OPTIONS`, `DELETE` or `TRACE`. Clients of the proxy request HTTPS pages with `CONNECT`. The methods are defined in [RFC 9110](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#name-methods).

arguments.name: action
arguments.description:
What the proxy does with the response to a matching request.
- `allow` (default) - Store the response when it can be cached.
- `deny` - Do not store the response. [`/ip/proxy/inserts`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/ip/proxy/inserts) and [`/ip/proxy/lookups`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/ip/proxy/lookups) count such requests as `denied`.

flags.name: X
flags.description: disabled. The rule is not used. New rules are created enabled.

readOnlyArguments.name: hits
readOnlyArguments.description: Number of requests the rule matched. Reset it with [`reset-counters`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/ip/proxy/cache/reset-counters) or [`reset-counters-all`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/ip/proxy/cache/reset-counters-all).

readOnlyArguments.name: file-size
readOnlyArguments.description: Size of the object, in KiB.

readOnlyArguments.name: last-modified
readOnlyArguments.description: Date the proxy stored the object. It is not the `Last-Modified` header of the response.

readOnlyArguments.name: last-modified-time
readOnlyArguments.description: Time the proxy stored the object.

flags.name: S

flags.name: C

readOnlyArguments.description: Address of the server.

State of the connection, for example:

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: Whether the web proxy runs. Default: no.

arguments.name: src-address
arguments.description: Source address of the connections the proxy opens to servers. It must be an address of the router; otherwise, and when it is not set, the router uses the source address chosen by routing. Default: `::` (not set).

arguments.name: port
arguments.description: TCP port the proxy listens on, or several ports as a comma-separated list, for example `8080,3128`. The proxy listens on all IPv4 and IPv6 addresses of the router, so protect the port with firewall rules. To tell the ports apart in rules, use `local-port` in the access, cache and direct lists. Default: 8080.

arguments.name: anonymous
arguments.description:
Whether the proxy tells the server about the client.
- `no` (default) - Add `Via: 1.1 (Mikrotik HttpProxy)`, `X-Forwarded-For: ` and `X-Proxy-ID` to the requests sent to servers. When a request arrives with `Via` and `X-Forwarded-For` already set, for example from another proxy, the proxy adds its entries to them.
- `yes` - Send none of these headers.

arguments.name: parent-proxy
arguments.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address of another proxy that receives the requests, HTTPS (`CONNECT`) requests included, except those that [`/ip/proxy/direct`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/ip/proxy/direct/) sends directly to the server. The parent proxy is used only when `parent-proxy-port` is not 0. When the parent proxy cannot be reached, the client gets an error page; the router does not fall back to a direct connection. Default: `::` (none).

arguments.name: parent-proxy-port
arguments.description: TCP port of the parent proxy. With 0, no parent proxy is used, even when `parent-proxy` is set. Default: 0.

arguments.name: cache-administrator
arguments.description: Name or email address shown on the error pages of the proxy as a `mailto:` link, the `$(admin)` variable of the error page template (see [`reset-html`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/ip/proxy/reset-html)). Default: webmaster.

arguments.name: max-cache-size
arguments.description:
Largest total size of the cache, in KiB.
- `unlimited` (default) - No limit. A RAM cache can then use most of the router's free memory, so set a limit on a router that runs other services.
- `none` - Do not cache.
- A number - Limit in KiB.

arguments.name: max-cache-object-size
arguments.description: Largest response the proxy stores in the cache, in KiB. Larger responses reach the client without being stored. Default: 2048KiB.

arguments.name: cache-on-disk
arguments.description:
Where the proxy keeps the cache.
- `no` (default) - In RAM.
- `yes` - On the storage of the router, in the store named by `cache-path`, which `/file` shows with the type `web-proxy store`.

arguments.name: max-client-connections
arguments.description: Largest number of client connections the proxy serves at the same time. Further requests wait until a connection is free. Default: 600.

arguments.name: max-server-connections
arguments.description: Default: 600.

arguments.name: max-fresh-time
arguments.description: Default: 3d.

arguments.name: serialize-connections
arguments.description: Default: no.

arguments.name: always-from-cache
arguments.description: Default: no.

arguments.name: cache-hit-dscp
arguments.description: DSCP value, 0 to 63, the router sets on the packets of responses it serves from the cache. Use it to recognise cache hits in queues and firewall rules. Default: 4.

arguments.name: cache-path
arguments.description: Name of the cache directory. With `cache-on-disk=yes`, the router creates it on its storage as a `web-proxy store`. A path, for example `usb1/web-proxy` on a disk, needs an existing directory; otherwise the router refuses it with `bad cache path`. It cannot be empty. Default: web-proxy.

readOnlyArguments.name: denied

arguments.name: sni
arguments.description: Host name the rule serves. It is compared with the server name (SNI) the client sends in the TLS handshake and must match it exactly; a wildcard such as `*.example.com` matches nothing. The router closes a connection whose server name matches no rule, and the `rproxy` log shows `no matching rule for `.

arguments.name: ip-address
arguments.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address of the server the requests are forwarded to. The router connects from its own address and forwards each request as HTTP/1.1. It keeps the `Host` header and adds `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Real-Ip` with the address of the client, `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, `X-Forwarded-Host` and `Forwarded`.

arguments.name: port
arguments.description: TCP port of the server. The router always connects with plain HTTP, also when the port is 443, so the server must accept HTTP on this port.

arguments.name: certificate
arguments.description: Certificate the router presents to clients of this rule, for example one issued for the `sni` host name. With `none`, the certificate of the `reverse-proxy` service in [`/ip/service`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/ip/service/) is used. When that is also `none`, the TLS handshake fails, and the `rproxy` log shows `certificate missing for rule `. Default: none.

flags.description: The rule was created by RouterOS for a container app with `use-https=yes` and a web interface (see [`/app`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/app/)). Its `sni` is the host name of the app URL, and its certificate is the one set in `/app/settings`.

arguments.name: port
arguments.description: TCP port the service listens on, `1..65535`. When another service already listens on the port, the entry becomes invalid (`I`). The default depends on the service: `ftp` 21, `ssh` 22, `telnet` 23, `www` 80, `www-ssl` 443, `winbox` 8291, `api` 8728, `api-ssl` 8729, `reverse-proxy` 443.

arguments.name: address
arguments.description: Deprecated name of `available-from`. A value set with `address` is written to `available-from`.

arguments.name: available-from
arguments.description: IPv4 and IPv6 prefixes of the clients allowed to use the service. A client from another address can still open the TCP connection, and the router then closes it without serving the client, so the port stays visible. To hide a service from untrusted networks, drop the traffic in the firewall input chain as well. Empty means any address. Default: empty.

arguments.name: certificate
arguments.description: Certificate the service presents to TLS clients. Applies to `www-ssl`, `api-ssl` and `reverse-proxy`. With `none`, `www-ssl` and `api-ssl` accept only anonymous Diffie-Hellman ciphers: the connection is encrypted, but the router does not prove its identity, and browsers and tools such as cURL cannot connect. Set a certificate for HTTPS. For `reverse-proxy`, the certificate is used by the rules that have none of their own (see [`/ip/reverse-proxy`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/ip/reverse-proxy)). Default: none.

arguments.name: ip-forward
arguments.description: Enable or disable packet forwarding between interfaces. Resets all configuration parameters to defaults according to [RFC 1812](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc1812) for routers.

arguments.name: send-redirects
arguments.description: Send ICMP redirects. Enable this on routers.

arguments.name: accept-source-route
arguments.description: Accept packets with the SRR option. Accepting source-routed (SSRR/LSRR) packets is a well-known spoofing/security risk and should be kept disabled unless required by the setup.

arguments.name: accept-redirects
arguments.description: Accept ICMP redirect messages. Enable on hosts and disable on routers.

arguments.name: secure-redirects
arguments.description: Accept ICMP redirect messages only for gateways listed in the default gateway list.

arguments.name: rp-filter
arguments.type: enum (no | strict | loose) { no:0, strict:1, loose:2 }
arguments.description:
Enable or disable source validation.
- `no` - Do not validate source addresses.
- `strict` - Strict mode as defined in [RFC 3704](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3704) Strict Reverse Path. Each incoming packet is tested against the FIB and if the interface is not the best reverse path, the packet check will fail. By default, failed packets are discarded.
- `loose` - Loose mode as defined in [RFC 3704](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3704) Loose Reverse Path. Each incoming packet's source address is tested against the FIB and if the source address is not reachable through any interface, the packet check will fail.
[RFC 3704](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3704) recommends enabling `strict` mode to prevent IP spoofing from DDoS attacks.
If you use asymmetric routing, complex routing, or VRRP, then `strict` mode will cause problems, enable `loose` mode instead.

arguments.name: ipv4-multipath-hash-policy
arguments.type: enum (l3 | l4 | l3-inner) { l3:0, l4:1, l3-inner:2 }
arguments.description:
IPv4 hash policy used for [ECMP](/docs/7.25/user-guides/routing-and-networking-protocols/routing-decision#multipath-ecmp-routes) routing.
- l3 - Layer-3 hashing of source and destination IP addresses.
- l3-inner - Layer-3 hashing, or inner layer-3 hashing if available.
- l4 - Layer-4 hashing of source and destination IP addresses, IP protocol, source port, and destination port.
With [L3 hardware offloading](/docs/7.25/bridging-and-switching/l3-hardware-offloading) enabled, hardware-forwarded ECMP uses the switch chip's own hash mask, which includes L4 ports for TCP/UDP; the configured policy is ignored. FastTrack-offloaded connections follow the kernel FIB lookup and may select a different nexthop. [FastPath](/docs/7.25/firewall-and-quality-of-service/packet-flow-in-routeros#fast-path) caches routes by L3.

arguments.name: tcp-syncookies
arguments.description: Send syncookies when the SYN backlog queue of a socket overflows. This helps prevent SYN flood attacks. However, syncookies violate the TCP protocol and prevent the use of TCP extensions, which can degrade some services (for example, SMTP relaying). This degradation may be visible to your clients and relays contacting you.

arguments.name: tcp-timestamps
arguments.type: enum (disabled | random-offset | enabled) { disabled:0, random-offset:1, enabled:2 }
arguments.description: Enable or disable TCP timestamps, or add a random offset to TCP timestamps (default behavior). Disabling timestamps can help reduce performance drop spikes.

arguments.name: max-neighbor-entries
arguments.description:
Sets Linux `gc_thresh3`. A maximum number of allowed neighbors in the ARP table. Default value depends on the installed amount of RAM. It is possible to set a higher value than the default, but it increases the risk of out-of-memory condition.
The default values for certain RAM sizes:
- 2048 for 64 MiB,
- 4096 for 128 MiB,
- 8192 for 256 MiB,
- 16384 for 512 MiB or higher.
The ARP cache stores ARP entries, and if some of these entries are incomplete, they can stay in the cache for an indefinite period of time. This will only happen if the number of entries in the cache is less than one-fourth of the maximum number allowed. The reason for this is to prevent the unnecessary running of the garbage-collector when the ARP table is not close to being full.

arguments.name: arp-timeout
arguments.description: Sets Linux `base_reachable_time` (`base_reachable_time_ms`) on all interfaces that use ARP. The initial validity of the ARP entry is picked from the interval [`timeout/2 - 3*timeout/2`] (default from 15s to 45s) after the neighbor was found. Can use postfix ms, s, m, h, d for milliseconds, seconds, minutes, hours, or days. If no postfix is set then seconds (s) are used. The parameter means how long a valid ARP record will be considered complete if no one communicates with the specific MAC/IP during this time. The parameter does not represent a time when an ARP entry is removed from the ARP cache (see `max-neighbor-entries` setting).

arguments.name: icmp-rate-limit
arguments.description: Limit the maximum rates for sending ICMP packets whose type matches icmp-rate-mask to specific targets. Value of `0` disables any limiting, other values indicate the minimum space between responses in milliseconds.

arguments.name: icmp-rate-mask
arguments.description: Mask of ICMP types for which rates are limited. For more information, see the [Linux man pages](http://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/icmp.7.html).

arguments.name: icmp-errors-use-inbound-interface-address
arguments.description: When enabled, send ICMP error message replies with a source address equal to the primary address of the receiving interface that caused the error. Use this for complex network debugging.

arguments.name: ipv4-high-fragment-thresh
arguments.description:
Sets the upper bound of memory (in bytes) the kernel may consume for all fragment reassembly queues combined (every interface and every flow). When the total memory used by the cache reaches this limit the kernel starts dropping newly arriving fragments, causing packets to be discarded. Raising the limit reduces the chance of drops under heavy fragmentation (e.g. high-throughput links with VPNs, or MTU-limited paths), but it also raises the maximum amount of RAM that can be used.
The default value depends on the installed amount of RAM:
- 512 KiB for 64 MiB of RAM,
- 1024 KiB for 128 MiB of RAM,
- 2048 KiB for 256 MiB of RAM,
- 4096 KiB for 512MiB of RAM,
- 16 MiB for 1 GiB of RAM,
- 32 MiB for 2 GiB of RAM or higher.

arguments.name: ipv4-fragment-time
arguments.description: Time in seconds to keep an IPv4 fragment in memory.

arguments.name: allow-fast-path
arguments.description: Allows [Fast Path](/docs/7.25/firewall-and-quality-of-service/packet-flow-in-routeros#fast-path)

readOnlyArguments.description: Amount of fast-pathed packets.

readOnlyArguments.name: ipv4-fast-path-bytes
readOnlyArguments.description: Amount of fast-pathed bytes.

readOnlyArguments.name: ipv4-fasttrack-packets
readOnlyArguments.description: Amount of fasttracked packets.

readOnlyArguments.name: ipv4-fasttrack-bytes
readOnlyArguments.description: Amount of fasttracked bytes.

- `yes` - the server is enabled.

In a rule that serves a folder or the requested name, a pattern such as `.*`, or an empty value, also matches names that lead out of the folder: use a pattern such as `[^/.][^/]*` that allows no slash and no leading dot.

arguments.description: Whether to add a default route (`::/0`) through the DHCPv6 server, or through the relay if the reply came through one. DHCPv6 itself does not provide a default gateway. Default: no.

arguments.description: Distance of the default route the client adds. Default: 1.

arguments.name: default-route-tables
arguments.description: Routing tables to add the default route to, as `table` or `table:distance` entries. `default` is the main routing table, or the VRF routing table when the client interface belongs to a VRF. Default: default.

arguments.name: use-peer-dns
arguments.description: Whether to accept the DNS servers advertised by the DHCPv6 server. Default: yes.

arguments.name: use-interface-duid
arguments.description: Whether to use a DUID generated from the MAC address of the client interface, instead of the router's DUID that the router's other DHCPv6 clients and its DHCPv6 server use. Default: no.

arguments.name: custom-duid
arguments.description: DUID to send instead of the generated one, in hex, for example `0x0003000102aabbccddee`. Overrides `use-interface-duid`.

arguments.name: validate-server-duid
arguments.description: Whether to check that the DUID sent by the DHCPv6 server is correctly formed. With `no`, an incorrectly formed server DUID is accepted, but its minimum length is still checked. Default: yes.

arguments.name: rapid-commit
arguments.description: Whether to ask for the two-message exchange (Solicit and Reply) with the Rapid Commit option. If the server does not use it, or with `no`, the four-message exchange (Solicit, Advertise, Request, Reply) is used. Default: yes.

arguments.description: Whether to accept Reconfigure messages from the DHCPv6 server. When enabled, the client says so in its Solicit, receives a reconfigure key, and renews immediately when the server sends a Reconfigure message. The RouterOS DHCPv6 server sends Reconfigure messages when its settings change and with the `send-reconfigure` command of the binding. Default: no.

arguments.description: Options the client sends, selected by name from `/ipv6/dhcp-client/option`. The predefined `fqdn` option sends the router's identity as the client's FQDN (option 39). Default: fqdn.

arguments.description: Name of the dynamic IPv6 pool the client creates from the received prefix, from which addresses can be assigned to other interfaces. The lifetime of the pool follows the prefix and is extended with each renewal. Applied only when a prefix is requested.

arguments.name: pool-prefix-length
arguments.description: Prefix length the pool hands out, for example `64`. It must be equal to or longer than the received prefix. When not set, the length is chosen automatically, for example 64 for a received /56. Applied only when a prefix is requested.

arguments.name: prefix-hint
arguments.description: Prefix or prefix length to suggest to the server, for example `::/60` to ask for a /60. The server does not have to follow it. `::/0` sends no hint. Default: ::/0.

- `pd-valid` - `1` when the prefix was obtained, `0` when it was lost; empty when the run is about the address.
- `pd-prefix` - The prefix, with its length.
- `na-valid` - `1` when the address was obtained, `0` when it was lost; empty when the run is about the prefix.
- `na-address` - The address.
- `options` - Array of the options received from the server, indexed by option code.

readOnlyArguments.name: status
readOnlyArguments.type: enum (stopped | searching... | requesting... | bound | renewing... | rebinding... | stopping... | declining... | error | idle | requesting-info... | confirming...)
readOnlyArguments.description:
Current state of the client:
- `searching...` - Sending Solicit messages and waiting for a server.
- `requesting...` - Requesting the offered address or prefix.
- `bound` - The client has its address or prefix.
- `renewing...` - Renewing with the server that gave the address or prefix.
- `rebinding...` - The server did not answer the renewal; asking any server.
- `requesting-info...` - Waiting for the reply to an Information-request (`request=info`).
- `idle` - The Information-request was answered (`request=info`).
- `confirming...` - Checking with a server that the address or prefix is still valid for the link.
- `declining...` - Declining an address.
- `stopping...` - Sending a Release message.
- `stopped` - The client is disabled.
- `error` - The client cannot run.

readOnlyArguments.name: status
readOnlyArguments.description:
State of the binding:
- `waiting` - A static binding that is not in use, or a dynamic binding that was used before. The server keeps a dynamic binding for 10 minutes so the old client can get it back; after that the prefix can be given to other clients.
- `offered` - The server answered a Solicit with an Advertise, but has not received the Request. The client has 2 minutes to request the binding.
- `bound` - The client uses the binding.

readOnlyArguments.name: expires-after
readOnlyArguments.description: Time until the binding expires.

readOnlyArguments.name: last-seen
readOnlyArguments.description: Time since the server last received a message from the client, or `never`.

readOnlyArguments.name: client-address
readOnlyArguments.description: IPv6 address the client sends from, usually its link-local address. The routes to the binding use it as the gateway.

readOnlyArguments.name: reconfigure-key
readOnlyArguments.description: Key the server gave the client for authenticating Reconfigure messages (`use-reconfigure`).

readOnlyArguments.name: reconfigure-last-sent
readOnlyArguments.description: Replay-detection counter of the last Reconfigure message sent to the client. It increases with every Reconfigure message.

readOnlyArguments.name: fqdn
readOnlyArguments.description: FQDN the client sent (option 39).

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: Name of the DHCPv6 server.

arguments.name: interface
arguments.description: Interface the DHCPv6 server listens on.

arguments.name: prefix-pool
arguments.description: IPv6 pool from which dynamic prefix bindings get their prefixes. With `static-only`, only static bindings are given out. Default: static-only.

arguments.name: address-pool
arguments.description: IPv6 pool from which dynamic address bindings get their addresses. The pool prefix length must be 128. With `static-only`, only static bindings are given out. Default: static-only.

arguments.name: lease-time
arguments.description: Lifetime of new and renewed bindings. Clients are told to renew after half of it and to rebind after 80% of it, and the preferred lifetime is 90% of it. Default: 3d.

arguments.name: rapid-commit
arguments.description: Whether to answer a Solicit that asks for Rapid Commit directly with a Reply (two-message exchange). With `no`, the server always answers with an Advertise first. Default: yes.

arguments.name: use-radius
arguments.description: Whether to use a RADIUS server for bindings: `no` (default), `yes` for authentication and accounting, or `accounting` for accounting only.

arguments.name: preference
arguments.description: Preference value sent in Advertise messages. Clients prefer the server with the highest value. Default: 255.

arguments.name: binding-script
arguments.description:
Script to run when a binding is bound and when it ends. It runs separately for each binding, and receives these variables:
- `bindingBound` - `1` when the binding was bound, otherwise `0`.
- `bindingServerName` - Name of the DHCPv6 server.
- `bindingDUID` - DUID of the client.
- `bindingAddress` - IPv6 address the client sends from, usually its link-local address.
- `bindingPrefix` - The delegated prefix, or the assigned address for an address binding.

arguments.name: dhcp-option
arguments.description: Options (`/ipv6/dhcp-server/option`) to send to clients, for example DNS servers (option 23).

arguments.name: insert-queue-before
arguments.description: Where to place the dynamic simple queues created for bindings with a `rate-limit`: `first` (default) at the top of `/queue/simple`, `bottom` at the end, or before the named queue.

arguments.name: parent-queue
arguments.description: Parent of the dynamic simple queues created for bindings with a `rate-limit`. Default: none.

arguments.name: route-distance
arguments.description: Distance of the routes the server adds to each delegated prefix and assigned address, through the client's link-local address. Default: 1.

arguments.name: allow-dual-stack-queue
arguments.description: Whether a binding and a DHCP lease of the same client share one dynamic simple queue, which then contains both the IPv6 and the IPv4 address. The client is recognized by its MAC address and DUID. The DHCP server must have this setting enabled as well. Default: yes.

arguments.name: use-reconfigure
arguments.description: Whether to send Reconfigure messages. When enabled, clients that accept them get a reconfigure key, and the server sends a Reconfigure message by itself: to all its bindings when `address-pool`, `lease-time` or `dhcp-option` change, and to a binding when the binding's settings change, so the clients renew; and a rebind request when the server or the binding's server is removed. The `send-reconfigure` command of the binding sends one manually. Default: no.

arguments.name: address-lists
arguments.description: IPv6 firewall address lists to which the prefix or address of each binding is added. The `address-lists` setting of a binding overrides this.

arguments.name: add-dns-entries
arguments.description: Whether to add a dynamic DNS entry (type AAAA) for each address binding. The entry name is the FQDN the client sends (option 39) followed by `add-dns-entries-suffix`, and its TTL is the lease time. Prefix bindings get no entry. Default: no.

arguments.name: add-dns-entries-suffix
arguments.description: Domain appended to the client name in the DNS entries created by `add-dns-entries`, for example `laptop.lan`. Default: lan.

arguments.name: ignore-ia-na-bindings
arguments.description: Whether to ignore address requests (IA_NA) and act as if the client's messages did not contain them, so only prefixes are handed out. Without it, a server with no address pool still answers each address request that no address is available, which can make a client that requests both keep asking. Default: no.

flags.name: D
flags.description: The DHCPv6 server was created dynamically.

flags.name: I
flags.description: The DHCPv6 server configuration is invalid.

readOnlyArguments.name: duid
readOnlyArguments.description: DUID of the server. The router uses the same DUID for its DHCPv6 clients.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: Name of the option, used where options are assigned.

arguments.name: code
arguments.description: DHCPv6 option code, for example 23 for DNS servers.

arguments.name: value
arguments.description: Value of the option, in the same syntax as DHCP server option values. An IPv6 address in quotes is sent as 16 bytes, for example `'2001:db8::53'`.

readOnlyArguments.name: raw-value
readOnlyArguments.description: The option value as it is sent, in hex.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: Name of the option set.

arguments.name: options
arguments.description: Options (`/ipv6/dhcp-server/option`) in the set.

arguments.name: list
arguments.description: Name of the address list. A new name creates the list. Rules match the list with `src-address-list` and `dst-address-list`.

arguments.name: address
arguments.description: An IPv6 address, a prefix or a DNS name. A prefix with host bits is stored as its network, and an address without a prefix length is stored as a /128. Ranges are not accepted (`is not a valid dns name`). For a DNS name, the router adds one dynamic entry for each AAAA record in the answer, with the name as the comment, and resolves the name again when the record expires. An address that is already in the list is refused with `already have such entry`.

arguments.name: timeout
arguments.description: Time after which the router removes the entry. An entry with a timeout is dynamic (`D`): it is not saved in the configuration or in exports, and a reboot clears it. The maximum is `35w3d13h13m56s`. Without a timeout, the entry stays until you remove it.

arguments.name: dynamic
arguments.description: With `yes`, the entry is dynamic (`D`) and has no timeout: it is not saved in the configuration and a reboot clears it. Default: no.

flags.name: X
flags.description: Disabled: the entry stays in the list but does not match.

flags.name: D
flags.description: Dynamic: the entry has a timeout or was added with `dynamic=yes`, by a firewall rule with a time or `none-dynamic`, from a resolved DNS name or by another feature (DNS, DHCP server). Dynamic entries are not saved in the configuration or in exports, and a reboot clears them.

readOnlyArguments.name: creation-time
readOnlyArguments.description: When the entry was created. A static entry keeps this time after a reboot; an imported entry gets the time of the import.

readOnlyArguments.name: protocol
readOnlyArguments.description: Connection protocol.

readOnlyArguments.name: src-address

readOnlyArguments.description: Source port of the connection.

readOnlyArguments.description: TCP connection state.

arguments.name: chain
arguments.description: Specifies to which chain the rule will be added. If the input does not match the name of an already defined chain, a new chain will be created.

arguments.name: action
arguments.type: enum (accept | jump | return | log | passthrough | add-src-to-address-list | add-dst-to-address-list | drop | reject | fasttrack-connection) { accept:0, jump:1, return:2, log:3, passthrough:4, add-src-to-address-list:5, add-dst-to-address-list:6, drop:10, reject:11, fasttrack-connection:45 }
arguments.description: Action to take if a packet is matched by the rule: `accept` - accept the packet. A packet is not passed to the next firewall rule. `add-dst-to-address-list` - add the destination address to the address list specified by the `address-list` parameter. `add-src-to-address-list` - add the source address to the address list specified by the `address-list` parameter. `drop` - drop the packet. `fasttrack-connection` - fasttrack the connection. `jump` - jump to the user-defined chain specified by the value of the `jump-target` parameter. `log` - add a message to the system log containing the following data: in-interface, out-interface, src-mac, protocol, src-ip:port->dst-ip:port, and length of the packet. After a packet is matched it is passed to the next rule in the list, similar to `passthrough`. `passthrough` - if a packet is matched by the rule, increase the counter and go to the next rule (useful for statistics). `reject` - reject the packet and send an ICMP response. `return` - passes control back to the chain from where the jump took place.

arguments.name: jump-target
arguments.description: Name of the target chain to jump to. Applicable only if `action=jump`.

arguments.name: reject-with
arguments.type: enum (icmp-no-route | icmp-admin-prohibited | icmp-not-neighbour | icmp-address-unreachable | icmp-port-unreachable | tcp-reset | icmp-err-src-routing-header | icmp-headers-too-long) { icmp-no-route:0, icmp-admin-prohibited:1, icmp-not-neighbour:2, icmp-address-unreachable:3, icmp-port-unreachable:4, tcp-reset:6, icmp-err-src-routing-header:7, icmp-headers-too-long:8 }
arguments.description:
Specifies the [ICMP error](https://www.iana.org/assignments/icmpv6-parameters/icmpv6-parameters.xhtml#icmpv6-parameters-codes-2) to be sent back if the packet is rejected. Applicable if `action=reject`.
- `icmp-no-route` - sends an ICMP address no-route message. ICMP type 1, code 0
- `icmp-admin-prohibited` - sends an ICMP address prohibited message. ICMP type 1, code 1
- `icmp-not-neighbour` - sends an ICMP address not-member message. ICMP type 1, code 2
- `icmp-address-unreachable` - sends an ICMP address unreachable message. ICMP type 1, code 3
- `icmp-port-unreachable` - sends an ICMP port unreachable message. ICMP type 1, code 4
- `tcp-reset` - sends an ICMP message resetting a TCP connection. ICMP type 1, code 6
- `icmp-err-src-routing-header` - sends an ICMP Error in Source Routing Header message. ICMP type 1, code 7
- `icmp-headers-too-long` - sends an ICMP Headers too long message. ICMP type 1, code 8

arguments.name: connection-nat-state
arguments.description: Matches connections that are source-natted, destination-natted, or both.

arguments.name: tls-host
arguments.description: Matches HTTPS traffic based on TLS SNI hostname. Accepts GLOB syntax for wildcard matching. The matcher will not be able to match the hostname if the TLS handshake frame is fragmented into multiple TCP segments.

arguments.name: connection-state
arguments.description: Interprets the connection tracking analytics data for a particular packet: `established` - a packet that belongs to an existing connection. `invalid` - a packet that does not have a determined state in connection tracking (usually severe out-of-order packets, packets with wrong sequence/ack number, or in case of resource over usage on the router). An invalid packet will not participate in NAT, and will still contain the original source IP address when routed. You should drop all `connection-state=invalid` packets in the firewall filter forward and input chains. `new` - the packet has started a new connection or is otherwise associated with a connection that has not seen packets in both directions. `related` - a packet that is related to, but not part of an existing connection, such as ICMP errors or a packet that begins an FTP data connection. `untracked` - a packet that was set to bypass connection tracking in firewall RAW tables.

arguments.name: connection-limit
arguments.description: Matches connections per address or address block after a given value is reached. You should use this together with `connection-state=new` and/or with `tcp-flags=syn` because the matcher is very resource-intensive.

arguments.name: protocol
arguments.description: Matches the particular IP protocol specified by protocol name or number.

arguments.name: src-address
arguments.description: Matches packets whose source is equal to the specified IP or falls into the specified IP range.

arguments.name: dst-address
arguments.description: Matches packets whose destination is equal to the specified IP or falls into the specified IP range.

arguments.name: src-address-list
arguments.description: Matches the source address of a packet against a user-defined address list. Supports only one list.

arguments.name: dst-address-list
arguments.description: Matches the destination address of a packet against a user-defined address list. Supports only one list.

arguments.name: address-list
arguments.description: Name of the address list to be used. Applicable if the action is `add-dst-to-address-list` or `add-src-to-address-list`.

arguments.name: address-list-timeout
arguments.description:
How long the address stays in `address-list` after the `add-src-to-address-list` or `add-dst-to-address-list` action adds it. With a time, the rule adds a dynamic entry (`D`) that the router removes when the time ends; each new match of the rule resets the time to its full value. The maximum is `35w3d13h13m56s`. An address that is already a static entry in the list stays static.
- `none-dynamic` (`0s`) - Add a dynamic entry without a timeout. It is not saved in the configuration and a reboot clears it.
- `none-static` - Add a static entry. It is saved in the configuration and in exports, and stays after a reboot until you remove it.

arguments.name: src-address-type
arguments.description: Matches the source address type: `unicast` - an IP address used for point-to-point transmission. `local` - the address is assigned to one of the router's interfaces. `anycast` - a packet sent to the nearest node in a group. `multicast` - a packet is forwarded to a defined group of devices. `unreachable` - the address is unreachable.

arguments.name: dst-address-type
arguments.description: Matches the destination address type: `unicast` - an IP address used for point-to-point transmission. `local` - the destination address is assigned to one of the router's interfaces. `anycast` - a packet sent to the nearest node in a group. `multicast` - a packet is forwarded to a defined group of devices. `unreachable` - the address is unreachable.

arguments.name: headers
arguments.type:
super { !
, type: ubit (hop, dst, route, frag, ah, esp, none, proto)
, [mode] [ :enum (exact | contains) { exact:0, contains:1 }]
 }
arguments.description: Matches IPv6 next-header. Two types of header matching are possible controlled by the `mode` parameter: `contains` - soft matching, matches at least selected headers. `exact` - matches the exact set of selected headers.

arguments.name: tcp-flags
arguments.description: Matches the specified TCP flags: `ack` - acknowledging data. `cwr` - congestion window reduced. `ece` - ECN-echo flag (explicit congestion notification). `fin` - close connection. `psh` - push function. `rst` - reset connection. `syn` - new connection. `urg` - urgent data.

arguments.name: hop-limit
arguments.description: Matches the hop limit field in the IPv6 header.

arguments.name: connection-mark
arguments.description: Matches packets marked by the mangle facility with a particular connection mark. If `no-mark` is set, the rule will match any unmarked connection.

arguments.name: connection-type
arguments.description: Matches packets from related connections based on information from their connection tracking helpers. A relevant connection helper must be enabled under `/ip/firewall/service-port`.

arguments.name: connection-bytes
arguments.description: Matches packets only if a given amount of bytes has been transferred through the particular connection. 0 means infinity, for example `connection-bytes=2000000-0` means that the rule matches if more than 2MB has been transferred through the relevant connection.

arguments.name: connection-rate
arguments.description: Allows capturing traffic based on the present speed of the connection.

arguments.name: routing-mark
arguments.description: Matches packets marked by the mangle facility with a particular routing mark.

arguments.name: in-interface
arguments.description: Interface the packet has entered the router.

arguments.name: out-interface
arguments.description: Interface the packet is leaving the router.

arguments.name: in-interface-list
arguments.description: Set of interfaces defined in interface list. Works the same as `in-interface`.

arguments.name: out-interface-list
arguments.description: Set of interfaces defined in interface list. Works the same as `out-interface`.

arguments.name: in-bridge-port
arguments.description: Actual interface the packet has entered the router if the incoming interface is a bridge. Works only if `use-ip-firewall` is enabled in bridge settings.

arguments.name: out-bridge-port
arguments.description: Actual interface the packet leaves the router if the outgoing interface is a bridge. Works only if `use-ip-firewall` is enabled in bridge settings.

arguments.name: in-bridge-port-list
arguments.description: Set of interfaces defined in interface list. Works the same as `in-bridge-port`.

arguments.name: out-bridge-port-list
arguments.description: Set of interfaces defined in interface list. Works the same as `out-bridge-port`.

arguments.name: packet-mark
arguments.description: Matches packets marked by the mangle facility with a particular packet mark. If `no-mark` is set, the rule will match any unmarked packet.

arguments.name: src-port
arguments.description: List of source ports and ranges of source ports. Applicable only if the protocol is TCP or UDP.

arguments.name: dst-port
arguments.description: List of destination port numbers or port number ranges.

arguments.name: port
arguments.description: Matches if any (source or destination) port matches the specified list of ports or port ranges. Applicable only if `protocol` is TCP or UDP.

arguments.name: icmp-options
arguments.description: Matches ICMP type:code fields.

arguments.name: src-mac-address
arguments.description: Matches the source MAC address of the packet.

arguments.name: content
arguments.description: Matches packets that contain the specified text.

arguments.name: ingress-priority
arguments.description: Matches the priority of an ingress packet. Priority may be derived from VLAN, WMM, DSCP, or MPLS EXP bit.

arguments.name: priority
arguments.description: Matches the packet's priority after a new priority has been set. Priority may be derived from VLAN, WMM, DSCP, MPLS EXP bit, or from the priority set by using the set-priority action.

arguments.name: dscp
arguments.description: Matches the DSCP IP header field.

arguments.name: limit
arguments.type:
super { !
, count: num [1 .. 32000000000]
, [time] [ /time [1 .. ]]
, [burst] ,num [ .. 2000000000]
, [mode] [ :enum (packet | bit) { packet:0, bit:1 }]
 }
arguments.description:
Matches packets up to a limited rate (packet rate or bit rate). A rule with this matcher will match until this limit is reached. Parameters are written in the following format: `rate[/time],burst:mode`.
- `rate` - packet or bit count per time interval to match.
- `time` - specifies the time interval in which the packet or bit rate cannot be exceeded (optional, 1s will be used if not specified).
- `burst` - initial number of packets or bits to match: this number gets recharged every 10ms so burst should be at least 1/100 of a rate per second.
- `mode` - packet or bit mode.

arguments.name: dst-limit
arguments.description:
Matches packets until a given rate is exceeded. Rate is defined as packets per time interval. As opposed to the `limit` matcher, every flow has its own limit. Flow is defined by a mode parameter. Parameters are written in the following format: `rate[/time],burst,mode[/expire]`.
- `rate` - packet count per time interval per-flow to match.
- `time` - specifies the time interval in which the packet count rate per flow cannot be exceeded (optional, 1s will be used if not specified).
- `burst` - initial number of packets per flow to match: this number gets recharged by one every time/rate, up to this number.
- `mode` - specifies what unique fields define flow (src-address, dst-address, src-and-dst-address, dst-address-and-port, addresses-and-dst-port).
- `expire` - specifies interval after which flow with no packets will be allowed to be deleted (optional).

arguments.name: time
arguments.type:
super { !
, start: time [0 .. 86400]
, [end] -time [0 .. 86400]
, [day] ,ubit (sun, mon, tue, wed, thu, fri, sat)
 }
arguments.description: Creates a filter based on the packets' arrival time and date or, for locally generated packets, departure time and date. The matcher takes into account the time and timezone configured on the router.

arguments.name: random
arguments.description: Matches packets randomly with a given probability.

arguments.name: nth
arguments.description: Matches every nth packet: `nth=2,1` will match every first packet of 2, hence, 50% of all the traffic matched by the rule.

arguments.name: tcp-mss
arguments.description: Matches the TCP MSS value of an IP packet.

arguments.name: per-connection-classifier
arguments.description: PCC matcher allows dividing traffic into equal streams with the ability to keep packets with a specific set of options in one particular stream.

arguments.name: packet-size
arguments.description: Matches packets of specified size or size range in bytes.

arguments.name: log
arguments.description: Add a message to the system log containing the following data: in-interface, out-interface, src-mac, protocol, src-ip:port->dst-ip:port, and length of the packet. Allows logging of packets even if the action is not `log`, useful for debugging the firewall.

arguments.name: log-prefix
arguments.description: Adds the specified text at the beginning of every log message. Applicable if `action=log` or `log=yes` is configured.

arguments.name: ipsec-policy
arguments.description:
Matches the policy used by IPsec. Value is written in the following format: `direction, policy`.
- `in` - valid in the PREROUTING, INPUT, and FORWARD chains.
- `out` - valid in the POSTROUTING, OUTPUT, and FORWARD chains.
- `ipsec` - matches if the packet is subject to IPsec processing.
- `none` - matches packets that are not subject to IPsec processing.

arguments.name: chain
arguments.description: Specifies to which chain the rule will be added. If the input does not match the name of an already defined chain, a new chain will be created.

arguments.name: action
arguments.type: enum (accept | jump | return | log | passthrough | add-src-to-address-list | add-dst-to-address-list | sniff-tzsp | sniff-pc | drop | mark-packet | mark-connection | mark-routing | change-mss | change-dscp | set-priority | change-hop-limit | snpt | dnpt) { accept:0, jump:1, return:2, log:3, passthrough:4, add-src-to-address-list:5, add-dst-to-address-list:6, sniff-tzsp:7, sniff-pc:8, drop:10, mark-packet:30, mark-connection:31, mark-routing:36, change-mss:32, change-dscp:33, set-priority:37, change-hop-limit:38, snpt:43, dnpt:44 }
arguments.description:
Action to take if a packet is matched by the rule:
- `accept` - accept the packet. A packet is not passed to the next firewall rule.
- `add-dst-to-address-list` - add the destination address to the address list specified by the `address-list` parameter.
- `add-src-to-address-list` - add the source address to the address list specified by the `address-list` parameter.
- `change-dscp` - change the DSCP value of the packet.
- `change-hop-limit` - change the hop limit value of the packet.
- `change-mss` - change the MSS value of the packet.
- `dnpt` - perform destination IPv6 network prefix translation.
- `drop` - drop the packet.
- `jump` - jump to the user-defined chain specified by the value of the `jump-target` parameter.
- `log` - add a message to the system log containing the following data: in-interface, out-interface, src-mac, protocol, src-ip:port->dst-ip:port, and length of the packet. After a packet is matched it is passed to the next rule in the list, similar to `passthrough`.
- `mark-connection` - mark the connection with the specified `new-connection-mark`.
- `mark-packet` - mark the packet with the specified `new-packet-mark`.
- `mark-routing` - mark the packet for routing with the specified `new-routing-mark`.
- `passthrough` - if a packet is matched by the rule, increase the counter and go to the next rule (useful for statistics).
- `return` - passes control back to the chain from where the jump took place.
- `set-priority` - set the priority of the packet.
- `sniff-pc` - sniff the packet and send it to the specified Packet Capturer target.
- `sniff-tzsp` - sniff the packet and send it to the specified TZSP target.
- `snpt` - perform source IPv6 network prefix translation.

arguments.name: src-prefix
arguments.description: Source IPv6 prefix for SNPT/DNPT actions.

arguments.name: dst-prefix
arguments.description: Destination IPv6 prefix for SNPT/DNPT actions.

arguments.name: jump-target
arguments.description: Name of the target chain to jump to. Applicable only if `action=jump`.

arguments.name: new-packet-mark
arguments.description: Sets the new packet mark value.

arguments.name: new-connection-mark
arguments.description: Sets the new connection mark value.

arguments.name: new-routing-mark
arguments.description: Sets the new routing mark value.

arguments.name: new-mss
arguments.description: Sets the new MSS value.

arguments.name: new-dscp
arguments.description: Sets the new DSCP value.

arguments.name: new-priority
arguments.description: Sets the new priority value.

arguments.name: new-hop-limit

arguments.description:

arguments.name: dst-limit

- `rate` - packet or bit count per time interval to match.
- `time` - specifies the time interval in which the packet or bit rate cannot be exceeded (optional, 1s will be used if not specified).
- `burst` - initial number of packets or bits to match: this number gets recharged every 10ms so burst should be at least 1/100 of a rate per second.
- `mode` - packet or bit mode.

arguments.name: dst-limit
arguments.description:
Matches packets until a given rate is exceeded. Rate is defined as packets per time interval. As opposed to the `limit` matcher, every flow has its own limit. Flow is defined by a mode parameter. Parameters are written in the following format: `rate[/time],burst,mode[/expire]`.
- `rate` - packet count per time interval per-flow to match.
- `time` - specifies the time interval in which the packet count rate per flow cannot be exceeded (optional, 1s will be used if not specified).
- `burst` - initial number of packets per flow to match: this number gets recharged by one every time/rate, up to this number.
- `mode` - specifies what unique fields define flow (src-address, dst-address, src-and-dst-address, dst-address-and-port, addresses-and-dst-port).
- `expire` - specifies interval after which flow with no packets will be allowed to be deleted (optional).

How long the address stays in `address-list` after the `add-src-to-address-list` or `add-dst-to-address-list` action adds it. With a time, the rule adds a dynamic entry (`D`) that the router removes when the time ends; each new match of the rule resets the time to its full value. The maximum is `35w3d13h13m56s`. An address that is already a static entry in the list stays static.
- `none-dynamic` (`0s`) - Add a dynamic entry without a timeout. It is not saved in the configuration and a reboot clears it.

readOnlyArguments.name: status
readOnlyArguments.description:
Status of the cached entry:
- **noarp** - the neighbor entry is valid. RouterOS does not validate this entry, but it can be removed when its lifetime expires.
- **incomplete** - address resolution is in progress and the neighbor's link-layer address is not yet determined.
- **reachable** - the neighbor was reachable recently (within tens of seconds).
- **stale** - the neighbor is no longer known to be reachable. Will continue sending traffic to the neighbor before attempting reachability verification.
- **delay** - the neighbor is no longer known to be reachable, and traffic has recently been sent to the neighbor. RouterOS delays probes briefly to allow the upper-layer protocol to confirm reachability.
- **probe** - the neighbor is no longer known to be reachable and unicast Neighbor Solicitation probes are being sent to verify reachability.
- **failed** - RouterOS could not resolve the neighbor's MAC address using the Neighbor Discovery protocol.

arguments.name: multipath-hash-policy
arguments.type: enum (l3 | l4 | l3-inner) { l3:0, l4:1, l3-inner:2 }
arguments.description:
Specify the IPv6 hash policy for [ECMP](/docs/7.25/user-guides/routing-and-networking-protocols/routing-decision#multipath-ecmp-routes) routing:
- l3 - Layer-3 hashing of source IP, destination IP, flow label, and IP protocol.
- l3-inner - Layer-3 hashing or inner layer-3 hashing if available.
- l4 - Layer-4 hashing of source IP, destination IP, IP protocol, source port, and destination port.
With [L3 hardware offloading](/docs/7.25/bridging-and-switching/l3-hardware-offloading) enabled, hardware-forwarded ECMP uses the switch chip's own hash mask, which includes L4 ports for TCP/UDP; the configured policy is ignored. FastTrack-offloaded connections follow the kernel FIB lookup and may select a different nexthop. [FastPath](/docs/7.25/firewall-and-quality-of-service/packet-flow-in-routeros#fast-path) caches routes by L3.

Setting a value higher than the default increases the risk of out-of-memory conditions.

arguments.name: remote.address
arguments.description: Remote address used to connect and/or listen to.

arguments.name: remote.as
arguments.description: Remote AS number. If not specified BGP will determine remote AS automatically from the OPEN message.

arguments.name: remote.ttl
arguments.description: Acceptable minimum Time To Live, the hop limit for this TCP connection. For example, if 'ttl=255' then only single-hop neighbors will be able to establish the connection. This property only affects EBGP peers.

arguments.name: remote.allowed-as
arguments.description: Name of the num-list containing remote AS numbers that will be allowed to connect. Useful for dynamic peer configuration.

arguments.name: local.ttl
arguments.description: Time To Live (hop limit) that will be recorded in sent TCP packets.

arguments.name: local.role
arguments.type: enum (ibgp | ibgp-rr | ebgp | ebgp-provider | ebgp-rs | ebgp-rs-client | ebgp-customer | ebgp-peer)
arguments.description: BGP role. In most scenarios, set to iBGP or eBGP. For more information on BGP roles and route leak prevention, see [Route Leak Prevention](/docs/7.25/user-guides/routing-and-networking-protocols/unicast/bgp/route-leak-prevention) and the corresponding [RFC 9234](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc9234).

arguments.name: tcp-md5-key
arguments.description: Key used to authenticate the connection with TCP MD5 signature as described in [RFC 2385](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc2385). Leave empty to disable authentication.

arguments.name: connect
arguments.description: Whether to allow the router to initiate the connection.

arguments.name: listen
arguments.description: Enable listening for incoming connections. If `remote.address` is a host address and listening is enabled, close the listening socket after the first successful accept. If `remote.address` is a subnet and listening is enabled, the listening socket remains open after the first successful accept with a hard-coded limit of 256 open connections.

arguments.name: routing-table
arguments.description: Name of the routing table, to install routes in. Overrides the instance parameter.

arguments.name: vrf
arguments.description: Name of the VRF BGP connections operate on. By default uses the "main" routing table.

arguments.name: templates
arguments.description: List of template names that will be used to inherit parameter values from. Useful feature, to easily configure groups with overlapping configuration options.

arguments.name: as
arguments.description: A 32-bit BGP autonomous system number. The value accepts AS-Plain or AS-Dot formats. Override the instance ASN and configure BGP confederation using the following format: _`confederation_as/as`_. For example, if your AS is 34 and your confederation AS is 43, set `as=43/34`.

arguments.name: nexthop-choice
arguments.description: Affect outgoing **NEXT\_HOP** attribute selection. Next-hops set in filters always take precedence and are not changed on route reflection except when set in a filter. default - select the next-hop as described in [`RFC 4271`](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4271) force-self - use the local address of the interface that connects to the peer as the next-hop propagate - propagate received next-hop; if the route has a BGP **NEXT\_HOP** attribute, use it as the next-hop; otherwise, fall back to the default case

arguments.name: multihop
arguments.description: Enable when the remote peer is more than one hop away.This option affects outgoing next-hop selection as described in [`RFC 4271`](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4271) (for eBGP only, excluding iBGP peers local to the confederation). It also affects:Whether to accept connections from peers not in the same network (the remote address of the connection is used for this check)Whether to accept incoming routes with a NEXT\_HOP attribute not in the same network as the address used to establish the connectionThe target scope of routes installed from this peer; routes from multi-hop or iBGP peers resolve their next-hops through IGP routes by default

arguments.name: hold-time
arguments.description: Specifies the BGP Hold Time value to be used when negotiating with peers.According to the BGP specification, if the router does not receive successive **KEEPALIVE** and/or **UPDATE** and/or **NOTIFICATION** messages within the period specified in the Hold Time field of the **OPEN** message, then the BGP connection to the peer will be closed.The minimal `hold-time` value of both peers will be used (note that the special value 0 or 'infinity' is lower than any other value)* infinity \- never expire the connection and never send keepalive messages.

arguments.name: keepalive-time
arguments.description: The interval between keepalive messages, if not set then by default keepalive is 1/3 of the `hold-time`.

arguments.name: afi
arguments.type: ubit (ip, ipv6, l2vpn, l2vpn-cisco, vpnv4, vpnv6, evpn)
arguments.description: List of address families this peer can exchange routing information. The remote peer must support BGP capabilities optional parameter (they usually do) to negotiate any other address families than IP.

arguments.name: cisco-vpls-nlri-len-fmt
arguments.description: VPLS NLRI length format type. Used for compatibility with Cisco VPLS. \[\[Read more>>\]\].

arguments.name: output.remove-private-as
arguments.description: If set, then the BGP **AS-PATH** attribute is removed before sending out route updates if the attribute contains only private AS numbers.The removal process happens before routing filters are applied and before the local, AS number is prepended to the AS path.

arguments.name: output.as-override
arguments.description: If set, then all instances of the remote peer's AS number in the BGP **AS-PATH** attribute are replaced with the local AS number before sending a route update to that peer. Happens before routing filters and prepend.

arguments.name: use-bfd
arguments.description: Whether to use the BFD protocol for faster connection state detection.

arguments.name: save-to
arguments.description: Filename to save BGP protocol-specific packet content (Exported PDU) into pcap format. This method allows much simpler peer-specific packet capturing for debugging purposes.

arguments.name: output.add-path
arguments.description: Enable sending of additional paths for specified address families (BGP Addpath).

arguments.name: output.affinity
arguments.type: enum (main | alone | remote-as | instance | afi | vrf | input)
arguments.description: Configure output multicore processing. Read more in [Routing Protocol Multi-core Support](/docs/7.25/user-guides/routing-and-networking-protocols/routing-protocol-multi-core-support) article. **alone** - input and output of each session is processed in its own process, the most likely best option when there are a lot of cores and a lot of peers **afi, instance, vrf, remote-as** - try to run input/output of new session in process with similar parameters **main** - run input/output in the main process (could potentially increase performance on single-core even possibly on multicore devices with small amount of cores) **input** - run output in the same process as input (can be set only for output affinity)

arguments.name: output.redistribute
arguments.type: ubit (connected, static, rip, ospf, isis, bgp, vpn, dhcp, fantasy, modem, bgp-mpls-vpn, slaac)
arguments.description: Enable redistribution of specified route types.

arguments.name: output.filter-select
arguments.description: Name of the routing select chain to be used for prefix selection. If not specified, then default selection is used.

arguments.name: output.filter-chain
arguments.description: Name of the routing filter chain to be used on the output prefixes. If the chain is not specified, then BGP by default accepts everything.

arguments.name: output.network
arguments.description: Name of the address list used to send local networks. The network is sent only if a matching IGP route exists in the routing table and its **ORIGIN** attribute is set to IGP, other distribution methods have **ORIGIN** attribute set to INCOMPLETE.

arguments.name: output.default-originate
arguments.description: Specifies default route (0.0.0.0/0) distribution method. 'if-installed' option can be used to distribute default route only if corresponding IGP route present in the routing table.

arguments.name: output.default-prepend
arguments.description: How many times to prepend local ASN.

arguments.name: output.no-client-to-client-reflection
arguments.description: Disable client-to-client route reflection in Route Reflector setups.

arguments.name: output.no-early-cut
arguments.description: The early cut is the mechanism, to guess (based on default RFC behavior) what would happen with the sent NLRI when received by the remote peer. If the algorithm determines that the NLRI is going to be dropped, a peer will not even try to send it. However such behavior may not be desired in specific scenarios, then this option should be used to disable the early cut feature. Early cut works with eBGP sessions.

arguments.name: output.keep-sent-attributes
arguments.description: Store in memory sent prefix attributes, required for `dump-saved-advertisements` command to work. By default, sent-out prefixes are not stored to preserve the router's memory. An option should be enabled only for debugging purposes when necessary to see currently advertised prefixes.

arguments.name: input.add-path
arguments.description: Accept received additional paths (BGP Addpath) for specified address families.

arguments.name: input.affinity
arguments.type: enum (main | alone | remote-as | instance | afi | vrf)
arguments.description:
Configure input multi-core processing. Read more in [Routing Protocol Multi-core Support](/docs/7.25/user-guides/routing-and-networking-protocols/routing-protocol-multi-core-support) article.
- **alone** - input and output of each session are processed in its own process, most likely the best option when there are a lot of cores and a lot of peers.
- **afi, instance, vrf, remote-as** - try to run input/output of new session in process with similar parameters.
- **main** - run input/output in the main process (could potentially increase performance on single-core even possibly on multi-core devices with a small amount of cores).

arguments.description: Specifies the BGP Hold Time value to be used when negotiating with peers.According to the BGP specification, if the router does not receive successive **KEEPALIVE** and/or **UPDATE** and/or **NOTIFICATION** messages within the period specified in the Hold Time field of the **OPEN** message, then the BGP connection to the peer will be closed.The minimal `hold-time` value of both peers will be used (note that the special value 0 or 'infinity' is lower than any other value)* infinity \- never expire the connection and never send keepalive messages.

arguments.name: keepalive-time
arguments.description: The interval between keepalive messages, if not set then by default keepalive is 1/3 of the `hold-time`.

arguments.description: If set, then all instances of the remote peer's AS number in the BGP **AS-PATH** attribute are replaced with the local AS number before sending a route update to that peer. Happens before routing filters and prepend.

arguments.name: use-bfd

arguments.name: output.affinity
arguments.type: enum (main | alone | remote-as | instance | afi | vrf | input)
arguments.description: Configure output multicore processing. Read more in [Routing Protocol Multi-core Support](/docs/7.25/user-guides/routing-and-networking-protocols/routing-protocol-multi-core-support) article. **alone** - input and output of each session is processed in its own process, the most likely best option when there are a lot of cores and a lot of peers **afi, instance, vrf, remote-as** - try to run input/output of new session in process with similar parameters **main** - run input/output in the main process (could potentially increase performance on single-core even possibly on multicore devices with small amount of cores) **input** - run output in the same process as input (can be set only for output affinity)

arguments.name: output.network
arguments.description: Name of the address list used to send local networks. The network is sent only if a matching IGP route exists in the routing table and its **ORIGIN** attribute is set to IGP, other distribution methods have **ORIGIN** attribute set to INCOMPLETE.

arguments.name: output.default-originate
arguments.description: Specifies default route (0.0.0.0/0) distribution method. 'if-installed' option can be used to distribute default route only if corresponding IGP route present in the routing table.

arguments.name: output.default-prepend

arguments.name: output.no-client-to-client-reflection
arguments.description: Disable client-to-client route reflection in Route Reflector setups.

arguments.name: output.no-early-cut
arguments.description: The early cut is the mechanism, to guess (based on default RFC behavior) what would happen with the sent NLRI when received by the remote peer. If the algorithm determines that the NLRI is going to be dropped, a peer will not even try to send it. However such behavior may not be desired in specific scenarios, then this option should be used to disable the early cut feature. Early cut works with eBGP sessions.

arguments.name: output.keep-sent-attributes

arguments.name: input.affinity
arguments.type: enum (main | alone | remote-as | instance | afi | vrf)
arguments.description:
Configure input multi-core processing. Read more in [Routing Protocol Multi-core Support](/docs/7.25/user-guides/routing-and-networking-protocols/routing-protocol-multi-core-support) article.

arguments.description: OSPF area identifier. If the router has networks in more than one area, then an area with `area-id=0.0.0.0` (the backbone) must always be present. arguments.name: type
arguments.type: enum (broadcast | nbma | ptp | ptp-unnumbered | ptmp | ptmp-broadcast)
arguments.description:
The OSPF network type on this interface. Note that if interface configuration does not exist, the default network type is 'ptp' on PtP interfaces and 'broadcast' on all other interfaces.
- `broadcast` - Network type suitable for Ethernet and other multicast capable link layers. Elects designated router.
- `nbma` - Non-Broadcast Multiple Access. Protocol packets are sent to each neighbor's unicast address. Requires manual configuration of neighbors. Elects designated router.
- `ptp` - Suitable for networks that consist only of two nodes. Does not elect a designated router.
- `ptmp` - Point-to-Multipoint. Easier to configure than NBMA because it requires no manual configuration of a neighbor. Does not elect a designated router. This is the most robust network type and as such suitable for wireless networks, if 'broadcast' mode does not work well enough for them
- `ptp-unnumbered` - Works the same as ptp, except that the remote neighbor does not have an associated IP address to a specific PTP interface. For example, in case IP unnumbered is used on Cisco devices.

arguments.name: retransmit-interval
arguments.description: Time interval after which the lost link state advertisement will be resent. When a router sends a link state advertisement (LSA) to its neighbor, the LSA is kept until the acknowledgment is received. If the acknowledgment was not received in time (see transmit-delay), the router will try to retransmit the LSA.

arguments.name: transmit-delay
arguments.description: Link-state transmit delay is the estimated time it takes to transmit a link-state update packet on the interface.

arguments.name: hello-interval
arguments.description: The interval between **HELLO** packets that the router sends out on this interface. The smaller this interval is, the faster topological changes will be detected; the tradeoff is more OSPF protocol traffic. This value must be the same for all the routers on a specific network, otherwise, adjacency between them will not form.

arguments.name: dead-interval
arguments.description: Specifies the interval after which a neighbor is declared dead. This interval is advertised in hello packets. This value must be the same for all routers on a specific network, otherwise, adjacency between them will not form.

arguments.name: priority
arguments.description:
Router's priority. Used to determine the designated router in a broadcast network. The router with the highest priority value takes precedence. Priority value 0 means the router is not eligible to become a designated or backup designated router at all.
Default value is 128, keep this in mind if you had strict priorities set for DR/BDR election.

readOnlyArguments.name: state
readOnlyArguments.description:
- `Down` - No Hello packets have been received from a neighbor.
- `Attempt` - Applies only to NBMA clouds. The state indicates that no recent information was received from a neighbor.
- `Init` - Hello packet received from the neighbor, but bidirectional communication is not established (Its own RouterID is not listed in the Hello packet).
- `2-way` - This state indicates that bi-directional communication is established. DR and BDR elections occur during this state. Routers build adjacencies based on whether the router is DR or BDR, and the link is point-to-point or a virtual link.
- `ExStart` - Routers try to establish the initial sequence number that is used for the packet information exchange. The router with a higher ID becomes the master and starts the exchange.
- `Exchange` - Routers exchange database description (DD) packets.
- `Loading` - In this state, actual link state information is exchanged. Link State Request packets are sent to neighbors to request any new LSAs that were found during the Exchange state.
- `Full` - Adjacency is complete, and neighbor routers are fully adjacent. LSA information is synchronized between adjacent routers. Routers achieve the full state with their DR and BDR only. An exception is P2P links.

arguments.description: If enabled, the MikroTik cloud service looks up the time zone for the location of the router's public IP address at startup and applies it to `time-zone-name`, including daylight saving time. A `time-zone-name` set by hand while detection is on is kept until the next detection. Default: yes.

arguments.name: dst-delta
arguments.description: Offset added to `time-zone` while daylight saving time is active. Negative values are accepted, for time zones where the winter time is the daylight saving period. Default: +00:00.

arguments.name: dst-start
arguments.description: Local date and time when the daylight saving period starts. Daylight saving time is active from `dst-start` until `dst-end` exactly as configured: the period is a single date range and does not repeat in the following years. If `dst-start` is later than `dst-end`, daylight saving time is never active. Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. An omitted date or time part is reset, the date to 1970-01-01 or the time to 00:00:00 (for example `dst-start=05:00:00` gives `1970-01-01 05:00:00`), so always give both parts. Default: 1970-01-01 00:00:00.

arguments.name: dst-end
arguments.description: Local date and time when the daylight saving period ends. See `dst-start` for how the period is applied. Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS. An omitted date or time part is reset, the date to 1970-01-01 or the time to 00:00:00, so always give both parts. Default: 1970-01-01 00:00:00.

Where the messages go:
- `memory` - Keep them in a memory buffer named after the action, shown by `/log/print`. The buffer is empty after a reboot.
- `disk` - Write them to text files (`disk-file-name`).
- `echo` - Print them on open terminal sessions (`remember`).
- `remote` - Send them to a syslog server (`remote`).
- `email` - Send each message as an email (`email-to`).
- `script` - Run a script for each message (`script`).

To write to another disk or folder, put its name first, for example `usb1/log`. The folder must exist, otherwise the action is refused with `bad disk file name`. Two disk actions cannot use the same file name. Default: log.

arguments.name: disk-lines-per-file
arguments.description: Number of lines in each file before the action starts a new file, `1..65535`. Default: 1000.

arguments.name: disk-file-count
arguments.description: Number of files the action keeps, `1..65535`. When a new file starts and the count is reached, the oldest file and its entries are dropped. Default: 2.

arguments.name: remote-port

arguments.name: src-address
arguments.description: Source address of the packets sent to the syslog server. `0.0.0.0` leaves the choice to the router. Default: 0.0.0.0.

arguments.name: remote-log-format
arguments.description:
Format of the messages sent to the syslog server:
- `default` (default) - The topics and the message, ` `, without time or host name.
- `syslog` - BSD syslog (RFC 3164): `` (facility and severity), the time, the router's identity and the message. `syslog-facility`, `syslog-severity`, `syslog-time-format` and `add-topics-string` apply to it.
- `cef` - Common Event Format: the time and the router's identity, then `CEF:0|MikroTik|||` with the topics, a severity (`Low`, `Medium`, `High`) and the fields `dvchost`, `dvc` and `msg`, followed by the message's extra fields. Each message ends with `cef-event-delimiter`.

arguments.name: remote-protocol
arguments.description:
Transport to the syslog server. Every format works with every transport, and actions that send to the same address and port share one connection.
- `udp` (default) - One datagram per message. Messages sent while the server is unreachable are lost.
- `tcp` - A TCP connection. Up to 1000 messages logged while the server is unreachable, for all remote actions together, are kept in memory and sent when the connection is back; newer ones are dropped when the buffer is full. `default` and `syslog` messages have no delimiter in the stream; use `cef` over TCP.
- `tls` - The same as `tcp`, encrypted with TLS (`check-certificate`).

arguments.name: check-certificate
arguments.description: For `remote-protocol=tls`: whether to verify the server certificate against the trusted certificates in [`/certificate`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/certificate/). When the verification fails, the router does not send, logs `ssld,error client session, logging, remote IP: , ssl: no trusted CA certificate found` and tries again later. The name in the certificate is not compared with the server address, so trust only the CA of your log servers. Default: no.

arguments.name: cef-event-delimiter
arguments.description: Characters added at the end of every `cef` message, also over UDP. Default: `\r\n`.

arguments.name: syslog-time-format
arguments.description:
Time format of `syslog` messages:
- `bsd-syslog` (default) - `Oct 2 16:51:21`, the router's local time without the year.
- `iso8601` - `2026-10-02T16:51:21.726+03:00`, with milliseconds and the time zone offset.

arguments.description:
Facility in the `` of `syslog` messages, with its code:
- `kern` (0)
- `user` (1)
- `mail` (2)
- `daemon` (3) (default)
- `auth` (4)
- `syslog` (5)
