arguments.name: syslog-severity
arguments.type: enum (auto | emergency | alert | critical | error | warning | notice | info | debug) { auto:0xffffffff, emergency:0, alert:1, critical:2, error:3, warning:4, notice:5, info:6, debug:7 }
arguments.description:
Severity in the `` of `syslog` messages. A value other than `auto` sends every message with that severity.
- `auto` (default) - Take the severity from the message topics: `debug` 7, `info` 6, `warning` 4, `error` 3. A message with both `error` and `critical` gets 3.
- `emergency` (0) - System is unusable.
- `alert` (1) - Action must be taken immediately.
- `critical` (2) - Critical conditions.
- `error` (3) - Error conditions.
- `warning` (4) - Warning conditions.
- `notice` (5) - Significant condition.
- `info` (6) - Informational message.
- `debug` (7) - Debug message.

arguments.name: email-to

Each matching message is sent as its own email, with ` ` as the subject and the body, through the SMTP server, port, TLS mode and sender set in [`/tool/e-mail`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/tool/e-mail/). See [Email](/docs/7.25/system-information-and-utilities/e-mail).

arguments.name: email-cc
arguments.description: Additional recipients of the email action, in the CC header. Several addresses are allowed.

arguments.name: email-start-tls
arguments.description: Not used by the email action: STARTTLS follows the `tls` setting in [`/tool/e-mail`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/tool/e-mail/). Default: no.

arguments.name: remember
arguments.description: For `target=echo`: keep the messages logged while no terminal session is open and print them at the next login, once. Default: yes.

arguments.name: add-topics-string
arguments.description: For `remote-log-format=syslog`: put the topics in front of the message, ` `. The `default` format always contains the topics. Default: no.

arguments.name: script
arguments.description: For `target=script`: the script from [`/system/script`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/system/script/) to run for each matching message. The script gets the variables `$topics` (the topics as text, for example `system,error,critical`) and `$message`. Messages that match while the script is still running are skipped, and a message the script logs itself does not run it again.

arguments.name: vrf
arguments.description: VRF the remote action connects from. Default: main.

flags.description: One of the default actions: `memory`, `disk`, `echo` and `remote`.

arguments.name: topics
arguments.description:
Topics a message must carry to match. A message matches only when it has every topic listed: `topics=dhcp,debug` matches DHCP debug messages, not all DHCP messages and all debug messages. To log several topics, add one rule per topic. A rule without topics matches every message, debug messages included.
`!` before a topic excludes the messages that carry it, for example `topics=ntp,debug,!packet` logs NTP debug messages without the packet dumps. The topics are described on the [Log](/docs/7.25/diagnostics-monitoring-and-troubleshooting/log/#topics) page. The router accepts: `account`, `acme-client`, `amt`, `async`, `backup`, `bfd`, `bgp`, `bridge`, `calc`, `caps`, `certificate`, `clock`, `container`, `critical`, `ddns`, `debug`, `dhcp`, `discover`, `disk`, `dns`, `dot1x`, `dude`, `e-mail`, `error`, `event`, `evpn`, `fetch`, `firewall`, `gps`, `gsm`, `health`, `hotspot`, `igmp-proxy`, `info`, `interface`, `ipsec`, `iscsi`, `isdn`, `isis`, `kvm`, `l2tp`, `ldp`, `lora`, `lte`, `manager`, `mme`, `mpls`, `mqtt`, `mvrp`, `natpmp`, `netinstall`, `netwatch`, `ntp`, `ospf`, `ovpn`, `packet`, `pim`, `poe-in`, `poe-out`, `pon`, `ppp`, `pppoe`, `pptp`, `ptp`, `queue`, `radius`, `radvd`, `raw`, `read`, `rip`, `route`, `rpki`, `rproxy`, `rsvp`, `script`, `sertcp`, `simulator`, `smb`, `snmp`, `socksify`, `ssh`, `ssld`, `sstp`, `state`, `store`, `stp`, `system`, `telephony`, `tftp`, `timer`, `tr069`, `update`, `upnp`, `ups`, `vpls`, `vrrp`, `warning`, `watchdog`, `web-proxy`, `wiliot`, `wireguard`, `wireless`, `write`, `zerotier`.

arguments.name: prefix
arguments.description: Text added in front of every message the rule passes, as `: `. The prefix is part of the stored and of the sent message.

arguments.name: regex
arguments.description: Regular expression matched against the message text, followed by the message's extra fields. When it does not match, the rule does not pass the message, even when the topics match.

arguments.name: action
arguments.description: Action from [`/system/logging/action`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/system/logging/action/) that receives the matching messages. Every rule that matches passes the message to its own action; when two rules pass the same message to one action, the action receives it once. Default: memory.

flags.description: One of the four default rules: `info`, `error` and `warning` to `memory`, `critical` to `echo`.

arguments.name: show-at-login
arguments.description: Show the note after login: in interactive command-line sessions such as SSH or Telnet, right after the banner, and in WinBox. A command run over SSH without an interactive session does not show it. Default: yes.

arguments.name: show-at-cli-login
arguments.description: Also show the note before the Telnet login prompt, to anyone who connects, without authentication; independent of `show-at-login`. SSH does not show the note before login, and MAC Telnet asks for the credentials before it connects. Default: no.

arguments.name: note
arguments.description: Text of the note. `\n` starts a new line; `/system/note/edit note` opens the text in the built-in editor. A file named `sys-note.txt` in the root of the file storage replaces the note at the next startup, and the router then removes the file. Default: empty.

arguments.name: enabled
arguments.description: Enable the NTP client. When disabled, `status` is `stopped`. Default: no.

arguments.name: mode
arguments.description:
How the client gets time from servers:
- `unicast` (default) - Query each configured server directly.
- `broadcast` - Listen for time broadcast by servers on the local network.
- `multicast` - Listen for time multicast by servers on the local network.
- `manycast` - Discover servers by sending manycast queries to the local network.

arguments.name: servers
arguments.description: Space-separated list of NTP servers. Accepts IPv4 and IPv6 addresses (with `@vrf` or `%interface` suffixes where needed) and domain names, which are resolved with `/ip/dns`. Servers from this list also appear in the [servers](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/system/ntp/client/servers) list alongside dynamic entries.

arguments.name: vrf
arguments.description: VRF used for communication with the servers. Default: main.

readOnlyArguments.name: freq-drift
readOnlyArguments.description: Estimated frequency drift of the local clock, in PPM. Reset with [`reset-freq-drift`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/system/ntp/client/reset-freq-drift).

readOnlyArguments.name: status
readOnlyArguments.description:
Current client state:
- `stopped` - The client is disabled.
- `waiting` - No server is usable yet (no answer, or all peers rejected).
- `synchronized` - The clock is synchronized to `synced-server`.
- `using-local-clock` - The local clock is used as the reference (requires `use-local-clock=yes` in [`/system/ntp/server`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/system/ntp/server)).

readOnlyArguments.name: synced-server
readOnlyArguments.description: Address of the server the clock is synchronized to. `127.127.1.0` when the local clock is the reference.

readOnlyArguments.name: synced-stratum
readOnlyArguments.description: Stratum of the synchronized source. Primary servers are stratum 1; each synchronization step adds one.

readOnlyArguments.name: system-offset
readOnlyArguments.description: Offset between the local clock and the NTP source; shown in milliseconds when read with `print`.

arguments.name: address
arguments.description: IP address or domain name of the NTP server. IPv4 and IPv6 addresses can carry a `@vrf` suffix, and a link-local IPv6 address an `%interface` suffix. Domain names are resolved with `/ip/dns`; the result shows in `resolved-address`.

arguments.name: min-poll
arguments.description: Shortest interval between queries to this server, as the power of 2 in seconds (6 means every 64 s). Must be lower than `max-poll`. Range: 3..17. Default: 6.

arguments.name: max-poll
arguments.description: Longest interval between queries to this server, as the power of 2 in seconds (10 means every 1024 s). Range: 3..17. Default: 10.

arguments.name: iburst
arguments.description: When enabled, the client sends a burst of about a second interval queries right after the server is added, to get an initial estimate quickly. Default: yes.

arguments.name: auth-key
arguments.description: Key from [`/system/ntp/key`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/system/ntp/key) used to authenticate replies from this server. Replies that fail authentication are rejected (crypto NAK) and the client does not synchronize. Default: none.

arguments.name: key-val

readOnlyArguments.description: Peer address from the server list, or 127.127.1.0 for the local reference clock.

In this case, use the Backspace key instead.

arguments.name: boot-device
arguments.description:
Choose how RouterBOOT loads the operating system:
- **ethernet** — boot the device in Etherboot mode.
- **flash-boot** — enable Flashfig mode on startup. This setting reverts to NAND after a successful configuration change, or when a user logs into the board.
- **flash-boot-once-then-nand** — enable Flashfig mode on startup for a single boot only. After that, the setting resets to `nand-if-fail-then-ethernet`.
- **nand-if-fail-then-ethernet** — boot RouterOS from the NAND. If RouterOS does not boot, the device goes to Etherboot automatically. This is the default mode for devices straight out of the box.
- **nand-only** — boot RouterOS from the NAND.
- **try-ethernet-once-then-nand** — boot the device in Etherboot mode once. If no server is available, the device boots directly from the NAND or the storage type the device uses.
Etherboot mode is a special state for a MikroTik device. You can use it to reinstall the device with Netinstall.
You can put the device into Etherboot mode in several ways, depending on the device you use:
1. Press the Reset button and power on the device. Wait until the USR LED blinks, then stays on, and then turns off. Release the Reset button. The device boots in bootp mode to reinstall RouterOS with Netinstall.
2. Use the serial console. When the device boots, press and hold Control+E until the device shows that it is trying the bootp protocol.
3. Use the serial console. Press any key while the device boots, and then press O, 1, and X.

arguments.name: preboot-etherboot
arguments.description: Enables preboot-etherboot, which runs before the regular boot device. It works the same as `boot-device=etherboot`, but has an additional timeout value. If an IP address is not received from the Netinstall server before the timeout expires, the regular boot process starts.The preboot-etherboot configuration is stored in the BIOS, so downgrading RouterOS to an earlier version does not disable it. You can disable it from the RouterOS menu or by resetting the BIOS.Because etherboot accepts IP addresses from any BOOTP/DHCP server, use preboot-etherboot-server to start etherboot only when the address is received from the specified Netinstall server.

arguments.name: preboot-etherboot-server
arguments.description: Sets preboot-etherboot to accept an IP address only from the specified Netinstall server. This setting prevents unintentional etherboot from other BOOTP/DHCP servers.

arguments.name: etherboot-port
arguments.description: Selects the Etherboot/Netinstall interface. Applies only to CRS520, CRS804, and CRS812. The default port depends on the model.

arguments.name: boot-os
arguments.description: Changes the boot operating system for CRS3xx series switches.

arguments.name: regulatory-domain-ce
arguments.description: Enables extra-low TX power for high antenna gain devices (requires a reboot).

arguments.name: cpu-mode
arguments.description: Whether the CPU enters suspend mode on the HLT instruction. Most operating systems use the HLT instruction during the CPU idle cycle. When the CPU is in suspend mode, it consumes less power. In low-temperature conditions, you should choose the regular mode, so the overall system temperature is higher.

arguments.name: cpu-frequency
arguments.description: Use this option to change the CPU frequency of the device. Values depend on the model. To see the available options, press ? in RouterOS version 6 or F1 in RouterOS version 7 at this prompt.

arguments.name: memory-frequency
arguments.description: Use this option to change the memory frequency of the device. Values depend on the model. To see the available options, press ? in RouterOS version 6 or F1 in RouterOS version 7 at this prompt.

arguments.name: memory-data-rate
arguments.description: Use this option to change the memory data rate of the device. Values depend on the model. To see the available options, press ? in RouterOS version 6 or F1 in RouterOS version 7 at this prompt.

arguments.name: preferred-architecture
arguments.description: Specific setting for L009 devices. Updates the device to use the ARM64 architecture.

arguments.name: boot-protocol
arguments.description: The boot protocol to use:- **bootp** — the default option for booting RouterOS.- **dhcp** — used for OpenWrt and possibly other operating systems.

arguments.name: enable-jumper-reset
arguments.description: Disable this option to prevent an accidental settings reset through the onboard jumper.

arguments.name: force-backup-booter
arguments.description: Whether to use the backup RouterBOOT. This setting is useful only if the main loader is corrupted and cannot be fixed. Instead of booting the device with a pressed reset button (which loads the backup loader), you can use this setting to load it on every boot.

arguments.name: silent-boot
arguments.description: This option disables beeping sounds during boot (does not disable the RouterOS `beep` command).

arguments.name: disable-pci
arguments.description: Specific setting for devices with the MT7621 chip. Disables PCI.

arguments.name: gpio-function
arguments.description: Specific setting for M33 devices. By default, pins 12, 13, 15, and 16 are configured for use of the second `serial1` port. You can reassign them for GPIO use in the `/iot/gpio/digital` menu.

arguments.name: protected-routerboot
arguments.description:
Disables access to the RouterBOOT configuration over the serial console and prevents the reset button from changing boot mode (Netinstall is disabled). You can access RouterOS only with a known RouterOS user account with administrative privileges. You can disable this setting only from within RouterOS. If you lose the RouterOS password, recovery requires a full device reformat with the reset button timing procedure.
- **enabled** — secure mode. RouterOS is accessible only with a valid admin-level account. Serial input is ignored, Etherboot is disabled, and RouterBOOT settings cannot be changed.
- **disabled** — normal operation. RouterBOOT settings are accessible through the serial console, and the reset button can be used to enter Netinstall mode.

arguments.name: reformat-hold-button
arguments.description:
Defines the minimum time the reset button must be held at power-on to trigger a full device reformat. The hold time must be longer than this value, but shorter than `reformat-hold-button-max`. When triggered, the device performs a complete reset operation:
- RouterOS, all files, and configuration are permanently erased (NAND reformat).
- All RouterBOOT settings are reset to defaults.
- The device reboots.
- Because NAND boot fails, the device enters Etherboot automatically.
- Netinstall is required to reinstall RouterOS.
This operation is extremely dangerous. Use it only when all other access methods are unavailable. On some RouterBOARD devices, the reformat process can take more than 5 minutes. The device is ready for Netinstall after the reformat completes.

arguments.name: reformat-hold-button-max
arguments.description:
Defines the maximum time the reset button can be held during a reformat trigger. Works together with `reformat-hold-button` to create a precise time window.
For example, setting `reformat-hold-button=60s` and `reformat-hold-button-max=65s` requires the button to be held strictly between 60 and 65 seconds. This increases security by making accidental or guessed resets practically impossible. Introduced in RouterBOOT 3.38.3.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: Name of the entry. Log messages from its runs refer to it as `scheduler:`.

arguments.name: start-date
arguments.description: Date of the first run, in the format `YYYY-MM-DD` (years 1970..2106). Default: the date when the entry is added.

arguments.name: start-time
arguments.description:
Time of the first run:
- `HH:MM:SS` - The first run happens at this time on `start-date`.
- `startup` - Run during system startup. With `interval=0s` the entry runs once on each startup. With a non-zero `interval` the first run comes one interval after startup (or one interval after the entry is added while the router runs), not at startup itself.
Startup runs happen before interfaces are up and before the DHCP client has an address. Default: the time when the entry is added.

arguments.name: days
arguments.description:
Weekdays on which the entry runs:
- Unset (default) - The weekday is not considered. Runs follow `start-time` plus `interval` continuously across midnight.
- `always` - Every day, with day scheduling: each day starts again at `start-time`.
- `never` - The entry never runs.
- `sun`, `mon`, `tue`, `wed`, `thu`, `fri`, `sat` - Only on the listed days (comma-separated). Each matching day starts at `start-time` and repeats every `interval` until the end of that day. With `interval=0s` the entry runs once on each matching day.
An `interval` of `1d` or longer is not supported when `days` is set; the entry then shows the note `multi-day intervals are not supported with active day scheduling`.

arguments.name: interval
arguments.description: Time between runs. Runs happen at `start-date` and `start-time` plus whole multiples of the interval, so a start in the past aligns the schedule: `start-time=00:00:00 interval=1h` runs on every full hour. `0s` runs the entry once at `start-date` and `start-time` (with `days` set, once on each matching day). Default: 0s.

arguments.name: on-event
arguments.description: RouterOS commands to run, or the name of a `/system/script` entry. A script called by name runs with this entry's `policy`; it is refused with `not enough permissions` when the script's own policy has rights this entry's policy lacks. Default: empty.

arguments.name: policy
arguments.description: Policies the commands run with. Commands that need a missing policy fail with `not enough permissions (9)` in the log. See [script permissions](/docs/7.25/developer-guides/scripting/#script-permissions). Default: the policies of the user who adds the entry, limited to `ftp`, `reboot`, `read`, `write`, `policy`, `test`, `password`, `sniff`, `sensitive` and `romon`.

flags.name: X
flags.description: Disabled entry; it does not run until enabled.

readOnlyArguments.name: owner
readOnlyArguments.description: The user who added the entry.

readOnlyArguments.name: run-count
readOnlyArguments.description: Number of runs since the last startup. A reboot resets it to 0.

readOnlyArguments.name: next-run
readOnlyArguments.description: Date and time of the next run. Empty when no run is pending: an entry with `interval=0s` after its run, a `startup` entry with `interval=0s`, or an entry with `days=never`.

arguments.name: watch-address
arguments.description: Address the ping watchdog pings. The router sends six pings over `ping-timeout` and reboots when all six fail. `none` turns the ping watchdog off. Use an address that is reliably up and reached through the link to watch, such as the gateway or, for a VPN, the tunnel address of the far end. If it stays unreachable, the router reboots again after every boot, about every `ping-start-after-boot` plus `ping-timeout`. Default: none.

arguments.name: watchdog-timer
arguments.description: Whether the router reboots when the system is unresponsive for a minute. Default: yes.

arguments.name: ping-start-after-boot
arguments.description: Time after a boot before the ping watchdog sends its first ping to `watch-address`. On a router that has been up longer than this time, setting `watch-address` starts the pings at once. Set it longer than the watched link needs to come up after a boot. Older exports call it `no-ping-delay`. Default: 5m.

arguments.name: ping-timeout
arguments.description: Time over which the ping watchdog sends six pings to `watch-address`, one every `ping-timeout` divided by six. The router reboots when all six fail. Default: 1m.

arguments.name: automatic-supout
arguments.description: Whether the router writes `autosupout.rif` when the software fails. The previous file is renamed to `autosupout.old.rif`. A ping watchdog reboot does not write the file. Default: yes.

arguments.name: send-smtp-server

arguments.name: allocate-udp-ports-from
arguments.description: Beginning of UDP port range. The server and the client take the UDP ports for test data from this port upward, for example 2192 on the server and 2448 to 2467 for a client's 20 streams; firewalls must allow UDP to these ports in both directions. Range `1000..64000`. Default: 2000.

arguments.name: max-sessions
arguments.description: Maximal simultaneous test count. Tests are counted, not their connections. When this many tests run, a new test gets `can not connect`. A single test cannot use more connections than this value either: with `max-sessions=1`, only a test with `connection-count=1` runs. Range `1..1000`. Default: 100.

arguments.name: allowed-addresses4
arguments.description: IPv4 addresses or prefixes of the clients allowed to run tests. Empty allows every client. A client outside the list gets `can not connect`. Use this list to limit clients: a user's own `address` setting does not limit bandwidth test logins. Default: empty.

arguments.name: allowed-addresses6
arguments.description: IPv6 addresses or prefixes of the clients allowed to run tests, the same as `allowed-addresses4`. Default: empty.

arguments.name: address
arguments.description: IPv4 or IPv6 address of the server. A link-local IPv6 address needs the interface, for example `fe80::1%ether1`.

arguments.name: protocol
arguments.description:
Traffic to send:
- `udp` (default) - UDP packets of `local-udp-tx-size` and `remote-udp-tx-size` bytes; the receiver counts lost packets.
- `tcp` - TCP connections (`connection-count`); TCP adapts its rate to the path.

arguments.name: local-udp-tx-size
arguments.description: Size of the UDP packets the client sends, in bytes of the whole IP packet: 1500 sends a 1472-byte UDP payload. Values below 52 fail with `failure: size too small` over IPv4. Range `28..64000`. Default: 1500.

arguments.name: remote-udp-tx-size
arguments.description: Size of the UDP packets the server sends, counted the same way as `local-udp-tx-size`. Default: 1500.

arguments.name: direction
arguments.type: enum (receive | transmit | both) { receive:0x00000100, transmit:0x00000200, both:0x00000300 }
arguments.description:
Which side sends:
- `receive` (default) - The server sends, the client receives (`rx-*` values).
- `transmit` - The client sends, the server receives (`tx-*` values).
- `both` - Both sides send at the same time.

arguments.name: connection-count
arguments.description: Number of TCP connections, or of UDP streams with their own ports, that the test uses. Range `1..255`. Default: 20, or the number of CPU cores on routers with more than 20 cores.

arguments.name: local-tx-speed
arguments.description: Maximum rate the client sends at, in bits per second (suffixes such as `50M` work). Without it, the client sends as fast as it can: an unlimited UDP test floods for about the first second and then sends more than the receiver reports, so `lost-packets` stays above zero.

arguments.name: remote-tx-speed
arguments.description: Maximum rate the server sends at, in bits per second (suffixes such as `50M` work). Without it, the server sends as fast as it can.

arguments.name: user
arguments.description: User name on the server. The user's group needs both the `test` and `winbox` policies (see [`/user/group`](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/user/group)). Not needed when the server has `authenticate=no`.

arguments.name: password
arguments.description: Password of `user` on the server.

arguments.name: duration
arguments.description: How long the test runs. Without it, the test runs until you stop it, for example with Control+C.

arguments.name: random-data
arguments.description: Whether to fill the payload with random, incompressible data, so that links that compress traffic do not show a higher rate than they carry. It costs more CPU time on both sides. Default: no.

readOnlyArguments.name: status
readOnlyArguments.type: enum (connecting | can not start test | can not connect | remote is busy | test unsupported | running | disconnected | authentication failed | done testing) { connecting:0, can not start test:1, can not connect:2, remote is busy:3, test unsupported:4, running:5, disconnected:6, authentication failed:7, done testing:8 }
readOnlyArguments.description:
State of the test:
- `connecting` - The client is connecting to the server.
- `running` - The test runs.
- `done testing` - The test ended after `duration`.
- `authentication failed` - The server refused the user name or password, or no user was given while the server authenticates.
- `can not connect` - The server is disabled or not reachable, the client is not in its `allowed-addresses4`/`allowed-addresses6`, or `max-sessions` is reached.
- `disconnected` - The connection to the server ended during the test, also when the test uses more connections than the server's `max-sessions`.
Other values report that the server refused or could not start the test.

arguments.name: to
arguments.description: Destination email address. Several addresses are allowed, separated by commas; the router sends one message to all of them.

arguments.name: cc

arguments.name: file

arguments.name: user
arguments.description: Username used to authenticate to an SMTP server (AUTH PLAIN; unencrypted without TLS). If not specified, the value from the server configuration is used.

arguments.name: password
arguments.description: Password used to authenticate to an SMTP server. If not specified, the value from the server configuration is used.

arguments.name: tls
arguments.description:
TLS encryption mode. If not specified, the value from the server configuration is used:
- `no` - No TLS. The router does not send STARTTLS, also when the server offers it.
- `yes` - TLS from the start of the connection (implicit TLS, usually port 465).
- `starttls` - Upgrade the connection with STARTTLS (usually port 587). When the server does not offer STARTTLS, the send fails with `TLS not supported by server`; there is no fallback to an unencrypted connection.

arguments.name: certificate-verification
arguments.description:
TLS certificate validation. If not specified, the value from the server configuration is used:
- `no` - The router encrypts the connection but does not check the server's certificate.
- `yes` - Validates the certificate chain against the local certificate store, including the server name. The built-in trust store covers email by default.
- `yes-without-crl` - Validates the certificate without performing a CRL check.

arguments.name: url
arguments.description: Full URL of the resource, for example https://download.mikrotik.com/routeros/7.19/CHANGELOG or ftp://user:password@192.168.88.2/conf.rsc. The scheme selects the mode, and ftp/sftp URLs may carry the credentials. Can replace the separate address and src-path parameters. A VRF cannot be given inside the URL: in http://192.168.88.2@vrf1/ the part after @ is treated as the host name. Use the address parameter for VRF.

arguments.name: output
arguments.description:
Determines where the fetched data is stored.
- `none` - Do not store downloaded data.
- `file` (default) - Store downloaded data in a file (`dst-path`; with `url` and no `dst-path`, the file is named after the last part of the URL path).
- `user` - Store downloaded data in the `data` value of `as-value`, at most 64512 bytes (63 KiB); a longer body is cut without an error.
- `user-with-headers` - Store downloaded data in `data` (at most 20480 bytes, 20 KiB) and the response headers in `http-headers` (up to 44 KB).

arguments.name: http-method
arguments.type: enum (get | post | put | delete | head | patch)
arguments.description:
HTTP method of the request. PUT and PATCH without `http-data` send an empty body.
- `get` (default) - Request the resource.
- `post` - Send `http-data` to the resource.
- `put` - Send `http-data` as the new content of the resource.
- `delete` - Delete the resource.
- `head` - Request only the response headers.
- `patch` - Send `http-data` as a partial change of the resource.

arguments.name: http-auth-scheme
arguments.description: HTTP authentication scheme for `user` and `password`. With `basic`, the credentials are sent with the first request, without waiting for a challenge. Default: basic.

arguments.name: http-data
arguments.description: Request body for POST, PUT and PATCH. Maximum data limit is 64 KB. Without a `Content-Type` in `http-header-field`, the body is sent as `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`.

arguments.name: http-header-field
arguments.description: HTTP header fields and values, in the form of "h1:fff,h2:yyy": a comma starts the next header. To keep a comma inside one header value, escape it with two backslashes, e.g. "h:fff\\,yyy" sends `h: fff,yyy`. Fetch always sends `User-Agent: RouterOS ` and `Accept-Encoding: deflate, gzip`.

arguments.name: check-certificate
arguments.description:
TLS certificate validation for HTTPS.
- `no` (default) - Do not validate: fetch connects even to a server with an expired or self-signed certificate.
- `yes` - Validate the trust chain against the local certificate store, which includes a builtin trust store with public root certificates. An invalid certificate fails the fetch, for example with `failure: SSL: ssl: cert not valid (after: ... < now: ...)`.
- `yes-without-crl` - Validate the certificate without a CRL check.

arguments.name: certificate
arguments.description: Certificate from the certificate store used for server verification in HTTPS mode. Applicable only when `check-certificate` is enabled.

arguments.name: address
arguments.description: IP address or host name of the target device. Append @vrf_name to run the fetch operation within a specific VRF, or set only address=@vrf_name and let the url parameter supply the address.

arguments.name: src-address
arguments.description: Source IP address for establishing the connection. Applicable to HTTP, HTTPS, and SFTP modes only.

arguments.name: port
arguments.description: Port used for the connection. Default: the port of the mode (80 for `http`, 443 for `https`, 21 for `ftp`, 22 for `sftp`, 69 for `tftp`), or the port given in `url`.

arguments.name: mode
arguments.description:
Protocol used for the connection. With `url`, the protocol comes from the URL scheme.
- `http` (default) - HTTP.
- `https` - HTTP over TLS.
- `ftp` - FTP; download and upload.
- `tftp` - TFTP; download from a TFTP server, for example `/ip/tftp` on another router.
- `sftp` - SFTP over SSH; download and upload.

arguments.name: http-content-encoding
arguments.description: Compresses `http-data` with gzip or deflate and adds a matching `Content-Encoding` header. Only applicable to POST and PUT methods.

arguments.name: ip-type
arguments.description:
IP family preference when resolving domain names.
- `any` (default) - Use IPv4 or IPv6.
- `ipv4` - Use IPv4 only.
- `ipv6` - Use IPv6 only.

arguments.name: src-path
arguments.description: Path of the remote file; with `upload=yes`, the local file to upload.

arguments.name: dst-path
arguments.description: Destination path where the fetched file is saved; with `upload=yes`, the file name on the remote device. Without `dst-path`, a download is named after the last part of the URL path.

arguments.name: user
arguments.description: Username for authentication on the remote device. Without `user`, FTP logs in as `anonymous` and HTTP sends no credentials.

arguments.name: password
arguments.description: Password for `user`. With `user` and no `password`, HTTP sends an empty password.

arguments.name: host
arguments.description: Hostname or virtual hostname of the remote web server. Useful when the same IP serves multiple virtual hosts. For example, `address=manual.mikrotik.com host=forum.mikrotik.com`.

arguments.name: ascii
arguments.description: Enables ASCII mode for FTP/TFTP transfers. Default: no.

arguments.name: upload
arguments.description: Enables upload mode for FTP and SFTP transfers: `src-path` is the local file, and `dst-path` (or the path in `url`) the name on the remote device. HTTP uploads are not supported; use `http-method=put` with `http-data`. Default: no.

arguments.name: sftp-known-hosts-ignore
arguments.description: Skip SSH host key validation for this SFTP transfer. Has an effect when known-hosts-validation in /ip/ssh is enabled; without validation enabled, any host key is accepted. Default: no.

arguments.name: keep-result
arguments.description: Deprecated, use the output argument instead.

arguments.name: idle-timeout
arguments.description: Idle timeout since last read/write action. Default: 10s.

arguments.name: http-max-redirect-count
arguments.description: Maximum number of HTTP redirects that fetch follows. With the default of 2, a chain of two redirects is followed and a third fails the fetch with the received 3xx status. Default: 2.

arguments.name: http-percent-encoding
arguments.description: Percent-encodes every character in the request path except alphanumeric and `-._~/?^=:`. Default: no.

arguments.name: http-version
arguments.description: HTTP protocol version. HTTP2 is supported only on ARM64 and x86/CHR devices. Default: http1_1.

arguments.description:
Type of the probe (default value: **"simple"**) :

arguments.name: address
arguments.description: Host to ping: an IPv4 or IPv6 address, a DNS name, or a MAC address for MAC ping. The router resolves a name with its own DNS settings. An IPv6 link-local address and a MAC address take the interface as a suffix, for example `fe80::1%ether1` or `00:11:22:33:44:55%ether1`; a MAC ping without the suffix goes out of every interface. See [address flags](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/#address-flags).

arguments.name: interval
arguments.description: Time between two requests, `00:00:00.010..00:00:05` (10 ms to 5 s). A reply that arrives later than the interval counts as a timeout. Default: 1s.

arguments.name: size
arguments.description: Size of each request in bytes, as the whole IP packet including the IP header, `28..65535` for IPv4 and `48..65535` for IPv6. `size=1500` is a full-size packet on an Ethernet link. A request larger than the MTU of the outgoing interface is fragmented, unless `do-not-fragment` is set. Default: 56.

arguments.name: ttl
arguments.description: TTL of IPv4 requests and hop limit of IPv6 requests, `1..255`. Default: 255 for IPv4, 64 for IPv6.

arguments.name: dscp
arguments.description: Differentiated Services Code Point set in the IP header of the requests, `0..63`. For example, `dscp=46` (Expedited Forwarding) gives a ToS byte of `0xb8`. Default: 0.

arguments.name: do-not-fragment
arguments.description: Sets the Don't Fragment flag in the requests, so that they are not fragmented. A request larger than the path MTU then fails: a router with a smaller link on the path answers with the status `fragmentation needed and DF set`, and a request larger than the MTU of the outgoing interface, or than the path MTU the router has learned, fails with `packet too large and cannot be fragmented`. Use it with `size` to find the path MTU.

arguments.name: src-address
arguments.description: Source address of the requests. Use it when the test needs a particular address, for example the LAN address to test an IPsec site-to-site tunnel. Default: the `pref-src` of the route, otherwise the address of the outgoing interface.

arguments.name: arp-ping
arguments.description: Send ARP requests instead of ICMP echo requests, to reach a host on a directly connected IPv4 subnet that drops ICMP. Needs `interface`; without it the command fails with `interface needs to be specified for arp ping`. `host` shows the MAC address of the host that answered. Default: no.

arguments.name: count
arguments.description: Number of requests to send. Without it, ping runs until you stop it with Ctrl-C. In a script, the command returns the number of replies. Default: unlimited.

arguments.name: nd-ping
arguments.description: Use IPv6 Neighbor Discovery instead of ICMPv6 echo: the router sends Neighbor Solicitations (NS) and counts a Neighbor Advertisement (NA) as a reply. Works only for on-link IPv6 addresses; a global address also needs `interface`. Default: no.

arguments.name: interface
arguments.description: Interface the requests leave through. When no route through the interface covers the destination, the router treats the destination as directly connected there and sends ARP requests for it. Needed for `arp-ping`, for `nd-ping` to a global address and for IPv6 link-local addresses (or give the interface as the address suffix).

arguments.name: vrf
arguments.description: VRF the ping runs in. Only VRFs are accepted; a routing table that exists for policy routing is refused with `input does not match any value of vrf`. Default: main.

readOnlyArguments.name: seq
readOnlyArguments.description: Number of the request the row answers. Replies to a multicast request share one number.

readOnlyArguments.name: host
readOnlyArguments.type:
alt { ipv6-address: ip6Addr
, mac-address: macAddr
, ip-address: ipAddr
 }
readOnlyArguments.description: Address the reply came from: the host, or a router on the path that sent an ICMP error (see `status`). For ARP ping and MAC ping, the MAC address of the host that answered.

readOnlyArguments.name: size
readOnlyArguments.description: Size of the received packet in bytes. For an ICMP error from a router, the size of that message.

readOnlyArguments.name: ttl
readOnlyArguments.description: TTL (IPv4) or hop limit (IPv6) of the received packet. The difference from the value the sender used shows roughly how many routers the reply crossed.

readOnlyArguments.name: time
readOnlyArguments.description: Round-trip time: the time between sending the request and receiving the reply.

readOnlyArguments.name: status
readOnlyArguments.description:
Empty for an IPv4 reply, otherwise what happened to the request:
- `timeout` - No reply arrived within `interval`.
- `net unreachable` - The router in `host` has no route to the destination network, or a firewall rule there rejects the packet with the default `reject` action.
- `host unreachable` - The router in `host` reports that it cannot reach the host, or a firewall rule there rejects the packet with `icmp-host-unreachable`.
- `admin prohibited` - A firewall rule on the router in `host` rejects the packet.
- `TTL exceeded` - The TTL ran out on the router in `host`, usually because of a routing loop.
- `fragmentation needed and DF set` - The router in `host` has a link with a smaller MTU, and `do-not-fragment` is set.
- `packet too large and cannot be fragmented` - The request is larger than the MTU of the outgoing interface or than the learned path MTU, and `do-not-fragment` is set.
- `no route to host` - The router has no route to the address; for `nd-ping`, the address is not on a directly connected subnet.
- `echo reply` - An IPv6 echo reply.

readOnlyArguments.description: Number of requests sent.

readOnlyArguments.name: received
readOnlyArguments.description: Number of replies received.

readOnlyArguments.name: packet-loss
readOnlyArguments.description: Share of requests without a reply, in percent.

readOnlyArguments.name: min-rtt
readOnlyArguments.description: Shortest round-trip time of the run.

readOnlyArguments.name: avg-rtt
readOnlyArguments.description: Average round-trip time of the run.

readOnlyArguments.name: max-rtt
readOnlyArguments.description: Longest round-trip time of the run.

arguments.description: Disable or enable the RoMON feature.

arguments.name: address
arguments.description: IP or IPv6 address, or DNS name, of the destination. A name is resolved by the router's DNS resolver. See [address flags](/docs/7.25/cli-reference/#address-flags).

arguments.description: Sets the Don't Fragment flag in the IP header of the probes. With a large `size`, the router with a smaller link on the path answers with `fragmentation needed from `.

arguments.name: use-dns
arguments.description: Show the host names of the hops instead of their addresses. The names are looked up with reverse DNS queries through the router's DNS resolver; a hop without a reverse DNS record keeps its address. Default: no.

arguments.name: count
arguments.description: Number of rounds to run. Without `count`, the trace repeats every second until you stop it. Default: unlimited.

arguments.name: max-hops

arguments.name: protocol
arguments.description:
Type of the probes.

arguments.name: vrf
arguments.description: VRF whose routing table the probes use. Only VRFs are accepted; a routing table created for policy routing is refused. Default: main.

arguments.name: interface
arguments.description: Interface to send the probes out of. When no route through the interface covers the destination, the router treats the destination as directly connected there and sends ARP requests for it.

readOnlyArguments.name: sent

readOnlyArguments.name: last

readOnlyArguments.name: avg
readOnlyArguments.description: Average round-trip time of the answers from this hop.

readOnlyArguments.name: best
readOnlyArguments.description: Shortest round-trip time of the answers from this hop.

readOnlyArguments.name: worst
readOnlyArguments.description: Longest round-trip time of the answers from this hop.

readOnlyArguments.name: std-dev
readOnlyArguments.description: Standard deviation of the round-trip times of this hop: how much they vary from round to round.

readOnlyArguments.name: status
readOnlyArguments.description: Error the hop answered with instead of time exceeded, for example `network unreachable from 203.0.113.1` (no route, or a firewall `reject` with the default message), `host unreachable from 203.0.113.1`, `packet filtered from 203.0.113.1` (a firewall rejects the probe as administratively prohibited) or `fragmentation needed from 203.0.113.6` (with `do-not-fragment`, the probe is larger than the next link's MTU). The round ends at such a hop. Empty when the hop answers normally.

arguments.name: policy
arguments.description:
Rights granted to group members. Prefix a policy with `!` to revoke it. `add` revokes every policy it does not list, and a new group created without `policy` gets every policy negated (no rights). `set` changes only the policies it lists: `set policy=read,rest-api` on a group with `api` keeps `api`; `policy=!api` revokes it. Default: none.
- `local` - Log in on the local console.
- `telnet` - Log in through Telnet.
- `ssh` - Log in through SSH.
- `ftp` - Log in through FTP; allows reading, writing and erasing files (use together with `read` and `write`).
- `reboot` - Reboot the router.
- `read` - Read access to the router configuration.
- `write` - Write access to the configuration except user management; does not include `read`.
- `policy` - User management rights (use together with `write`); also allows seeing script variables created by other users (requires `test`) and designing WebFig skins (requires `sensitive`).
- `test` - Run ping, traceroute, bandwidth-test, wireless scan and snooper, fetch, email and other test tools.
- `winbox` - Log in through WinBox and use bandwidth-test authentication.
- `password` - Change the user's own password with `/password`.
- `web` - Log in through WebFig.
- `sniff` - Use the packet sniffer, torch and traffic generator.
- `sensitive` - See and change sensitive information.
- `api` - Access the router through the API.
- `romon` - Connect to the RoMON server.
- `rest-api` - Access the router through the REST API.
